t: Loudoun's final vote on its 12-month pause moves to Nov. 17
b: Deferred from Oct. 20 so staff can gather more information. The pause would be retroactive to Sept. 15; 33 data center and substation applications are active.
iw: Pause in the densest data center market

t: Charlotte's moratorium expires unless extended
b: City staff recommended extending it after a survey found 78% community opposition.
iw: Likely extension

t: Three Maine towns put data center bans or pauses to voters
b: North Berwick skipped a moratorium to let voters decide on a permanent ban.
iw: Possible permanent bans

t: Two Louisiana PSC seats are on the ballot
b: The commission will rule on Hyperion's second phase and large-load tariff policy.
iw: Regulator makeup at stake

t: Littleton weighs six-month moratorium on new data centers
b: The ordinance had a first reading in October. A public hearing and second reading are planned for Nov. 3. Staff would study land-use, energy, water, noise and infrastructure impacts.
iw: Possible pause if adopted, not yet decided

t: Emporia votes on a citizen ban of high-impact data centers
b: After a Lyon County judge ordered the question onto the ballot, the city set a vote on an initiative barring data centers above 10 MW or 100,000 gallons a day in every zoning district. The city argued zoning is not subject to initiative; legal review continues.
iw: Court-ordered vote on a citywide ban

t: El Dorado votes on a ten-year ban on high-impact data centers
b: City commissioners voted 5-0 on Aug. 25 to place a citizen initiative on the ballot after a Butler County judge found it legislative. The ordinance would bar high-impact data centers and larger battery storage systems for ten years, changeable only by another public vote.
iw: Decade-long ban that only voters could undo

t: Ottawa votes on a 25 MW data center ban while the case stays in court
b: A Franklin County judge ordered the Ottawa United initiative onto the November ballot after the city took no action on a certified petition with 658 signatures. The measure would ban data centers above 25 MW, aimed at a proposed 300-acre campus. Whether it is legislative and valid is undecided.
iw: Vote could block a pending 300-acre project

t: Hubbard votes on the only full city data center ban on Ohio's fall ballot
b: Voters in the Trumbull County city will decide a measure prohibiting data centers within city limits, with no megawatt threshold, the only outright municipal ban among Ohio's roughly 20 November questions. Neighboring Hubbard Township is separately drafting zoning rules that would bar them from residential and farm districts.
s: News From The States (Ohio Capital Journal)
iw: Permanent prohibition on the ballot

t: Grove City measure would require voter approval for large industrial projects
b: A citizen-initiated charter amendment backed by Protect Grove City would require a citywide vote on developments of 50 or more contiguous acres, over 20 MW peak demand or over 500,000 gallons of water a day. Conserve Ohio helped draft it as part of a statewide push.
iw: Would subject hyperscale projects to a public vote in a Columbus suburb

t: Ashville referendum on EdgeConneX data center terms set after court win
b: Voters will decide whether to uphold the village council's April emergency resolution approving terms for two EdgeConneX data centers and an 800 MW gas plant. The Ohio Supreme Court ruled Aug. 7 the council's emergency reasons were insufficient, reviving the petition the fiscal officer had blocked.
iw: Approved project terms now hinge on a village vote

t: Trenton's Issue 17 would cap data centers at 25 MW despite AWS build
b: A charter amendment forced onto the ballot by the Ohio Supreme Court would bar data centers over 25 MW. A 250 MW Amazon campus is already under construction in the industrial park and a second is proposed; the city says the first proceeds on existing permits.
iw: Would block AWS's second Trenton project

w: Conneaut, Defiance, Oregon, Piqua, Upper Sandusky voters
t: Five more Ohio cities vote on 25 MW caps or outright data center bans
b: Citizen charter amendments modeled on the stalled statewide initiative would bar data centers over 25 MW in Conneaut, Defiance and Oregon and prohibit construction in Piqua and Upper Sandusky. Piqua residents also filed petitions for a special election to void the city's power agreement for a Meta data center.
s: News From The States (Ohio Capital Journal)
iw: Permanent local limits spreading beyond central Ohio

t: Monroeville advisory vote and Perry guarantee rule round out Ohio's ballot
b: Monroeville voters will answer a non-binding question on whether officials should allow data center development in the village. Perry voters will decide whether hyperscale developers seeking special tax incentives must post financial guarantees, as Meta funds a nuclear expansion at the nearby Perry plant.
iw: Softer measures that still raise local hurdles

t: Adams County townships vote on zoning as Amazon eyes 1,300 MW site
b: Citizen initiatives would establish zoning in unincorporated Monroe and Sprigg townships to protect their rural character. Amazon is evaluating about 1,000 acres in Sprigg Township near Manchester for a $10 billion campus that an AES Ohio filing says could draw 1,300 MW, roughly 30 times the county's usage.
iw: First zoning in townships targeted for a hyperscale project

t: Bloomington Township voters weigh an advisory call for a hyperscale data center moratorium
b: Electors at a June 1 special township meeting voted 111-0 to put the nonbinding question on the Nov. 3 ballot proposed by petitioner Zach Gittrich. It asks whether voters want a moratorium on large-scale data centers in the city, without specifying a length. The city's pause ends in November.
iw: Advisory only, but a signal to a council writing rules

t: Joliet Township asks voters whether the city council should approve AI data centers
b: The advisory question on the Nov. 3 ballot asks: Should the Joliet City Council approve construction of AI data centers? It follows the council's March approval of the 795-acre Joliet Technology Center and a pending residents' lawsuit. Similar nonbinding questions appear in Madison County townships, Morgan County and Bloomington.
iw: Nonbinding, but a referendum on the state's largest approval

t: Pulaski County may vote to override the veto
b: The rules would require conditional use permits, setbacks and noise caps with no AVAIO carve-out.
iw: Possible new rules

t: Aurora to vote on indefinite data center moratorium after neighbors protest Trident project
b: A mayor-backed proposal would stop new applications until regulations are adopted but would not affect the pending Trident project. The Oct. 19 vote was delayed to Oct. 26 because two supporters could not attend.
iw: Indefinite pause on new applications in a major metro city

t: Harmony Township to vote on 24-month freeze on data centers and energy projects
b: Supervisors scheduled a hearing and vote on six separate two-year moratoria covering data centers, solar, wind, battery storage, gas generation and transmission lines. Minnkota Power and Xcel Energy, through a county commissioner, warned the freeze could cost tens of millions and threaten reliability; an attorney argued the notice was defective.
iw: Two-year freeze would stall a 540 MW campus

t: Champaign County set to bar tax abatements and NDAs for hyperscale data centers
b: A resolution clearing the committee of the whole unanimously Oct. 13 bars negotiating tax abatements, payments in lieu of taxes or other concessions for hyperscale data centers; a companion ordinance bans county officials from signing nondisclosure agreements. The full board votes Oct. 22; the county pause runs to April 2027.
iw: County incentives off the table even after its pause ends

t: Clackamas County unanimously pauses data centers in unincorporated areas for 120 days
b: Commissioners voted unanimously after hearings on Oct. 21 and 22. The pause takes effect immediately and gives staff time to study water, utility costs, land use and whether any ban is appropriate.
iw: Four-month stop on new projects in unincorporated county land.

t: Archbald unanimously denies the 14-building Wildcat Ridge campus
b: The 578-acre plan included 588 diesel backup generators. After nine hearings, council rejected it; an appeal is expected. Four more campuses are proposed in the borough.
iw: Hyperscale campus denied

t: Memphis mayor orders a data center rules plan within 90 days
b: Shelby County commissioners are weighing competing regulations and a 12-month moratorium.
iw: Rules coming

w: Missoula County Planning, Development and Sustainability
t: Missoula County study finds data center risks justify its moratorium
b: The draft emergency study released Oct. 21 cites electricity demand and costs, noise, wildlife and residential compatibility, and recommends stronger zoning. The county may extend the pause past July 8, 2027. A permanent ban is unlikely under the Right to Compute Act.
iw: Points to stricter zoning and a possible second year of pause

t: Somerset County requires data centers to make 150% of their own power
b: Unanimous ordinance also sets 1,000-foot setbacks from homes. No project had been filed.
iw: Very demanding power rule

t: Advocates count 110 New Jersey towns with data center bans
b: The group is pressing Gov. Sherrill for a three-year statewide moratorium.
iw: Breadth of local bans

t: Memphis rejects an 18-month pause, then passes a 135-day one
b: The longer moratorium failed 6–6 after weeks of protests. The shorter pause comes with land-use standards; xAI's Colossus expansion drove the fight.
iw: Short pause in a major hub

t: Volusia County bans data centers of 50 MW or more
b: Applies in unincorporated areas, citing the aquifer and sinkholes. Smaller projects face extra review.
iw: Permanent county ban

t: Broward County moves toward a one-year moratorium
b: Unanimous vote to begin the process for unincorporated areas.
iw: Likely county pause

t: Little Rock rejects a data center moratorium on a 4–4 tie again
b: A six-month pause failed by the same vote as an 18-month one in August.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Colorado PUC holds public hearing on Xcel's large-load data center tariff
b: The commission heard public comment on Xcel's proposal to make very large power users cover the grid costs of serving them. Five days earlier, activists delivered a petition with almost 5,000 signatures urging stronger customer protections.
iw: Tariff would shift grid costs onto large users like data centers

t: Brighton adopts one-year data center moratorium on second reading
b: After a first-reading vote Oct. 6, the day after a developer withdrew a 2.5-million-square-foot rezoning application, the council approved the ordinance again Oct. 20, the Denver Gazette reports. The pause runs one year from its effective date and can be extended 90 days. The effective date is unconfirmed.
iw: New applications frozen for a year in a growing metro city

t: Crowley calls for a pause on data centers during the DNR's statewide review
b: At a Madison stop the Democratic nominee said construction should pause while the DNR completes the environmental analysis due in January 2028, reversing his earlier opposition to a moratorium. Tiffany responded that his DNR would enforce strict standards before permits, without endorsing a pause.
iw: A leading candidate now backs a statewide pause of up to 15 months

t: Former Madison mayor: neither governor candidate is serious on data centers
b: In his Citizen Dave column, Cieslewicz argues Crowley and Tiffany attack each other's past support while offering only modest measures. He backs repealing the sales tax exemption but doubts either would deliver against business and union opposition, and says siting is mostly a local land-use call.
iw: Commentary; no direct business effect

t: Wisconsin Rapids rejects PNK Group's paper mill data center permit 7-0
b: The council denied the conditional use permit after the developer missed extended deadlines to complete its April application and the planning commission recommended denial in September. Residents cited noise and energy costs; the mayor said he is not against all data centers but wants it done right.
iw: Hyperscale project killed after a six-month fight

t: Florence County pauses data center land uses for up to 18 months
b: The board unanimously adopted a moratorium giving its zoning committee up to 18 months, or longer if needed, to revise the comprehensive plan and update zoning and land use rules for data centers.
iw: Border county closed to data center uses while rules are written

t: Ohio Supreme Court lets Lordstown reject data center filed before moratorium
b: Justices unanimously denied Bristolville 25 Developer's bid to force Lordstown to keep reviewing a site plan for four data centers submitted weeks before the village's November 2025 ban. Because preliminary steps were incomplete, the village had no duty to act once its moratorium, now extended through 2026, took effect.
iw: Court confirms local moratoriums can stop in-progress applications

w: Interim AI and Data Center Committee
t: North Dakota lawmakers outline 2027 data center bill on power, water, decommissioning
b: Rep. Anna Novak presented a draft requiring developers to bring their own power without shifting costs to ratepayers, use closed-loop cooling and bond for decommissioning. Other members proposed narrowing the sales tax exemption to computing equipment and requiring every county to adopt a data center ordinance. No votes were taken.
iw: Cost, cooling and bonding mandates taking shape for 2027

t: Judge upholds Ottawa citizen ban as legislative, clearing November vote
b: Judge Eric Godderz denied the city's motion to dismiss, ruling the Ottawa United initiative barring data centers above 25 MW for ten years is a new law rather than an administrative act, so it proceeds under the state initiative statute. Voters decide Nov. 3.
iw: Court removes the last legal obstacle to a decade-long ban

t: Montgomery County advances data center setbacks and limits
b: Approved 17–4: 500-foot residential setbacks plus noise, site size and utility capacity rules, returning in November.
iw: New siting limits

t: Boone signs an agreement with Lightedge for a possible data center
b: A step toward hosting a facility in a region full of pauses.
iw: Local welcome

t: Governor nominees favor local say and NDA limits, not new state rules
b: In their Brainerd debate both candidates said communities should decide on data centers and neither backed broad new regulation. Demuth cited the 2025 ratepayer law passed under her speakership; Klobuchar blamed House Republicans for killing an NDA ban she would revive.
iw: Neither nominee proposes a pause or new mandates

t: St. Cloud sets Nov. 16 hearing on hyperscale data center ordinance
b: The council agreed without opposition to a public hearing on rules requiring data centers to use city water, sit at least 1,320 feet from roads and residential zoning, submit land use, traffic, noise, environmental and community impact studies, and file decommissioning plans. The planning commission recommended the package.
iw: Quarter-mile setbacks and five studies proposed

t: Cincinnati takes public input on permanent data center zoning rules
b: At an in-person meeting after a virtual session Oct. 1, residents asked whether the city could say no. Draft zoning recommendations setting allowed districts and size limits are due in November, with targets of Jan. 15 for the Planning Commission and Feb. 2 for council, before the interim overlay lapses.
iw: Permanent discretionary review likely by early 2027

t: Farm Bureau column opposes easier eminent domain for data center projects
b: In a Columbus Dispatch guest column, the Farm Bureau's executive vice president argues proposals to expand quick-take eminent domain would make it easier to seize farmland for data centers and related pipelines and transmission lines, and that landowners should keep judicial review and fair compensation.
iw: Farm lobby weighing in on land-taking for data center infrastructure

t: Rockford drafts data center rules: closed-loop cooling, noise studies, paid upgrades
b: Proposed standards would make data centers a distinct zoning use and require water-conserving cooling, generator air permits, noise studies, buffers near homes and schools, utility confirmation of power, developer-funded infrastructure backed by a 110 percent letter of credit and decommissioning plans. A council committee took the first step.
iw: Detailed cost and disclosure conditions coming before the pause ends

t: Pitt County starts process toward a one-year data center moratorium
b: Commissioners voted unanimously to begin considering a one-year pause. Staff are to draft an ordinance by Oct. 30, with public hearings to follow and a final vote expected Nov. 16.
iw: Possible one-year pause, not yet enacted.

t: Warmington calls Ayotte's budget-based moratorium too slow
b: Both candidates for governor favor freezing new data center permits. Ayotte says she opposes the Bow and Nottingham proposals; Warmington argues a pause in next year's budget could come after a big project lands.
iw: Pause likely whoever wins

t: Leesburg march calls for a statewide data center moratorium
b: Part of a series of rallies organized with the Chesapeake Climate Action Network.
iw: Organized pressure for a state pause

t: Moratorium bills stack up for Virginia's 2027 session
b: SB 843 from Sens. Perry and Roem would block data center permits from July 2027 to July 2030. Del. Shin and Sen. Sturtevant have their own versions.
iw: Possible statewide pause in 2027

t: Hearing on Project Jupiter's air permit set for Dec. 7 in Sunland Park
b: Hearing Officer James Browning, a retired federal judge, scheduled the hearing to begin Dec. 7, with the first day for public comment. He also set Oct. 26 and Oct. 29 sessions on a motion to dismiss and on discovery.
iw: Key power-source permit decision still months away

t: Sierra Club settlement commits DNR to a statewide data center impact study
b: Settling a July lawsuit over permits for the Port Washington campus, the DNR will analyze cumulative effects of planned AI data centers on water, air, climate, energy and bills by Jan. 31, 2028, with public hearings. Vantage pays for the study; Lighthouse permits stand and no permitting pause is imposed.
iw: Study without a pause; existing permits untouched

t: Gilchrist says he opposes the Saline Township data center Whitmer championed
b: The lieutenant governor, now running for secretary of state, told a Detroit business luncheon he does not support the Oracle-OpenAI campus, criticized corporate bullying and litigation against small communities, and noted he skipped the June groundbreaking Whitmer attended with Sam Altman.
iw: Administration's number two breaks with the governor

t: Bayh makes data centers a centerpiece of Indiana secretary of state bid
b: Democrat Beau Bayh's advertising has focused on data centers and government corruption, which a Free Press Indiana poll identified as voters' top concern. The Bellwether survey of 839 likely voters put Bayh at 43% to Republican Max Engling's 35%, with 69% opposing new data centers.
iw: Statewide Democratic campaign built around data center backlash

t: Bloomington's draft rules would require special use permits for hyperscale data centers
b: The draft sorts data centers into accessory, commercial (under 10 acres and 10 MW) and hyperscale tiers. Hyperscale projects need a special use permit; all must file operations, decommissioning, electricity and water plans and meet noise limits. Hearings run through Nov. 16; council action is expected Nov. 23.
iw: Permanent permit hurdles replacing the temporary pause

t: Stratos developer files new water-right application with Utah regulators
b: O'Leary Digital asked the state to move existing irrigation water rights to the Stratos campus, saying use would fall below current farm use. A 20-day protest period follows public advertising. Two earlier applications were withdrawn after heavy protests.
iw: Necessary water step, but protests are expected

t: Poll: nearly 70% of Indiana voters oppose new data centers
b: A Bellwether Research survey of 839 likely voters taken Oct. 8–11 found 69% somewhat or strongly oppose building new data centers and 18% support them, with opposition up sharply from a year earlier. Gov. Braun, a data center backer, sat at 38% approval.
iw: Opposition now dominant in a pro-development state

t: Johnson County extends data center moratorium to August 2027
b: Supervisors voted 5-0 to add nine months to the pause on rezonings, permits and construction in unincorporated areas, which was set to expire Nov. 8. Staff said they are midstream on an ordinance covering water, parking and road impacts. No project has been proposed.
iw: Pause stretched to nearly two years

t: Pettis County halts large projects until economic and environmental studies finish
b: The temporary moratorium covers non-residential developments on at least 30 acres of unincorporated land or worth at least $5 million, with no fixed end date; it lifts once the commission reviews an economic development study, an environmental impact study, or both. No specific project was identified.
iw: Open-ended pause tied to studies

t: Reason says Ramaswamy's data center moratorium is a dodge from criticizing Trump
b: The column argues the Republican nominee, a self-described national libertarian, is targeting data centers and property taxes to avoid addressing tariffs and war, and that his proposed statewide moratorium is more restrictive than Trump's own pro-data-center stance.
iw: National libertarian outlet breaking with GOP nominee on moratorium

t: Meta revealed behind a 1.2 GW Mason County campus
b: A think tank estimates the project could get about $50 million a year in tax breaks. Residents had objected to secrecy.
iw: Major project under scrutiny

t: Attorney general says substantial share of Project Jupiter permit comments were not genuine
b: Torrez reviewed 17,419 comments: about 60% were one pro-project form letter from roughly 9,000 internet addresses, mostly with out-of-state phone numbers. About 4,700, mostly opposed, came from 17 connections. He advised NMED to consider reopening comment.
iw: Permit comment record, mostly pro-project, under investigation

t: Mayes hears data center complaints at Mesa town hall, floats community vote
b: Mayes said she would back a law requiring a community vote on data centers and that Prop. 207 does not stop her from filing a nuisance suit. Many speakers focused on the Ahwatukee campus. She promised another town hall there.
iw: Pressure for a state pause or local votes

t: Crowley says he would absolutely sign a repeal of data center tax breaks
b: The Democratic nominee for governor, previously noncommittal, told a Madison audience he would sign a repeal of the sales and use tax exemption. Republican Tom Tiffany had already called for ending the subsidy while labeling Crowley a data center ally in ads.
iw: Incentive repeal now backed by both nominees

t: Capitol protest demands oversight before data center projects advance
b: Demonstrators organized by Libertarian governor candidate Anthony Hudson rallied in Lansing for stronger review of data center projects before approval, the latest in a series of Capitol protests this year.
iw: Opposition now spans all parties in the governor race

w: No Dirty Data Centers MN coalition
t: Nine-group coalition launches data center voter guide before election
b: CURE, Clean Water Action, the Sierra Club North Star Chapter and six other groups published MN Data Center Voter, a nonpartisan site with explainers on health, water, energy and taxpayer impacts, questions for candidates and the policy proposals under debate.
iw: Organized opposition mobilizing voters

t: Both Iowa governor nominees say data center tax breaks should end
b: In the Sioux City debate, Republican Zach Lahn called for state rules making data centers cover their power costs and protect water and for letting counties impose moratoriums, citing $500 million in Cedar Rapids abatements for 30 jobs. Democrat Rob Sand pressed a ban on NDAs.
iw: Bipartisan consensus against incentives

t: Google drops Hermantown tax abatement request ahead of permit votes
b: City officials said Google will no longer seek the 28-year abatement proposed in April. Google instead offers a $210 million parent-company guarantee for decommissioning and strict liability for well damage. The planning commission reviewed the special use permit Oct. 20; the council votes Oct. 26.
iw: Developer concedes incentives to keep project moving

t: South Berwick adopts a 180-day pause for facilities over 10,000 sq ft
b: Retroactive to July 14. It expires just before the state's recommendations are due Jan. 29, 2027.
iw: Low size threshold

t: Westfield denies a permit extension for the Servistar hyperscale campus
b: The unanimous vote lets the 2021 special permit lapse at the end of October, likely ending what would have been New England's largest data center. Servistar never bought the land; it has 20 days to appeal.
iw: Major proposal likely ends

t: Howell Township extends data center moratorium another six months
b: Trustees voted unanimously to extend a pause first imposed in November 2025 and already extended in May, pushing it past its Nov. 20 expiration into 2027 while they finish a roughly 30-page permanent ordinance. New applications remain barred, though waivers can be requested.
iw: Pause extended at a site Meta had eyed

t: Slotkin calls for a data center pause, breaks with Whitmer
b: Speaking at a University of Chicago event, Michigan's senator said data centers should be paused so communities can decide whether to host them and weigh water and power use. She said Gov. Whitmer's support is not what the people want.
iw: Senior Democrat joins calls for a pause

t: Developer pitches $140 million in benefits to head off Harmony Township moratorium
b: Geronimo Power said its 540 MW Harmony Energy Park would deliver $100 million in property taxes, $20 million in payments to residents and a $20 million community fund, plus a 150 percent home value guarantee. Its CEO launched a petition urging supervisors to reject a proposed 24-month moratorium.
iw: Industry counteroffer against a pending township pause

t: Minneapolis advances data center zoning to replace moratorium expiring Nov. 21
b: The commission forwarded the city's first data-center-specific zoning, which limits facilities to two downtown districts, lowers the allowed server space, adds a zoning review step and design rules. The zoning committee takes it up Nov. 6 and the full council Nov. 12, days before the six-month pause lapses.
iw: Permanent location and size limits replacing the pause

t: Hubbard Township weighs zoning barring data centers from residential and farm land
b: At a packed hearing, trustees read a Trumbull County Zoning Commission recommendation adding restrictions to a nine-page data center resolution, including a ban in residential, agricultural, conservation and floodplain districts. Residents wanted an outright ban, citing PFAS and water concerns. No vote was taken; the next hearing is Oct. 27.
iw: Would confine projects to industrial zones near Lordstown

t: Environmental council urges Indiana communities to pause, plan and protect
b: The Indiana Capital Chronicle commentary proposes studying energy, water and cost impacts before approvals, ordinances setting clean-energy and transparency expectations, and enforceable agreements with third-party monitoring. It cites $561 million in 2025 sales tax exemptions for Amazon and data centers extending coal use.
iw: Environmental group's framework for local pauses

t: Quad Cities business paper says Iowa cities need facts and candor on data centers
b: Following the Iowa League of Cities conference, the editorial endorses the league's decision tool and argues developers should disclose water use, power demand and tax terms before projects reach council agendas, with cities making that a condition of incentives. It cites Clinton's proposed 1,100-acre QTS campus.
iw: Business press conditioning support on early disclosure

t: Bills for 2027 include a statewide pause and an end to tax breaks
b: One would pause construction through 2028; others would repeal or move up the exemption's expiration.
iw: Renewed pressure in 2027

w: Digital Realty and De Soto residents
t: Digital Realty offers De Soto households $1,000 a year as petition grows
b: The developer of a 300-acre campus proposed a $20 million community fund paying each household up to $1,000 annually for ten years toward property tax or utility bills. Neighbors who launched a petition against the project reported more than 400 signatures. A TIF hearing is set for Nov. 19.
iw: Benefit package meets rising petition opposition

t: Mayes asks regulators to investigate whether APS customers subsidized data centers
b: Citing an outside analysis alleging $587 million in power costs shifted to other customers, Mayes urged a public probe before APS's $608.7 million increase is approved. APS and the Corporation Commission dispute the analysis.
iw: Could delay or shrink rate decisions tied to large users

t: Phoenix posts early-morning inspectors at Ahwatukee data center site after complaints
b: The city said it would station inspectors before legal start times and secured contractor commitments to cut noise, such as moving truck traffic and limiting early deliveries. Construction hours return to 7 a.m.-7 p.m. weekdays on Oct. 16.
iw: Added enforcement on one project, no change to its approval

t: Bucksport adopts a six-month data center moratorium
b: The 5–2 vote covers all data centers, not just large ones. At least two data center firms have eyed the mostly vacant former Verso paper mill, though none has applied.
iw: Six-month town pause

t: Utah State survey: about three-quarters of residents oppose new data centers
b: A statewide August survey of nearly 900 adults found 75.8% oppose or strongly oppose building more data centers, with opposition higher nearer home. Water use was the top concern, and most were dissatisfied with state officials' handling.
iw: Broad opposition adds pressure on officials

w: Phil Weiser (D) and Victor Marx (R), governor candidates
t: Weiser and Marx outline data center views at Colorado Chamber forum
b: Weiser said data centers should meet clean-energy and water criteria, protect ratepayers, and not be forced on communities. Marx called for a common-sense approach that attracts investment, protects ratepayers and leaves decisions to local governments.
iw: Both support some guardrails; details differ

t: Study finds a data center construction ban beats Ohio's status quo
b: A Columbus firm's cost-benefit analysis ran 10,000 simulations of five scenarios for 2027–2034. The status quo scored a 1.04 benefit-cost ratio, versus 2.7 for a construction ban and 2.9 for self-generation with mostly renewables, because ratepayer costs fall while existing jobs stay. Results hinge on employment assumptions.
iw: Analytical ammunition for ban supporters weeks before the vote

t: Entergy discloses Meta will use 4,500 MW as hearing opens
b: Entergy has a settlement with regulators' staff; opponents say ratepayers could be left with plant costs after Meta's 20-year contract.
iw: Approval expected

t: Tooele planning commission tables data center ordinance after four-hour hearing
b: The commission voted unanimously to table draft Chapter 34 until a data center is defined, after residents delivered a letter with more than 900 signatures. The county said the council will not accept a data center application until the chapter is complete.
iw: Local rules delayed a third time amid opposition

t: Grand Junction advances one-year moratorium on data centers of one megawatt or more
b: Council approved the first reading on Oct. 7. The pause would last up to 365 days or until code changes pass. A public hearing and final vote were scheduled for Oct. 21; the outcome was not confirmed.
iw: Low threshold, so most projects would be covered

t: Denver names 26-member working group to recommend data center rules
b: Members were picked from more than 250 applicants and include residents, unions, utilities, industry and academics. The one-year moratorium runs to May 2027 and could be extended. Officials have not ruled out a ban.
iw: Ongoing uncertainty over whether new projects will be allowed

t: Wentzville adopts six-month ban on data centers over 5 MW
b: Aldermen voted 6-0 to pause projects of at least 5 MW or 100,000 square feet and to bar existing facilities from expanding without board approval. The mayor said no projects are pending and the pause can be renewed. It follows St. Charles County's July moratorium.
iw: Another St. Charles County city closes

t: IURC approves AES Indiana's $737 million plan to power Google's Monrovia campus
b: Regulators unanimously approved batteries, solar and lines for a 390 MW Google data center in Morgan County, the first filing under the 2025 large-load law. Google pays $32.3 million for direct facilities; $73.8 million in network upgrades enters rate base over Citizens Action Coalition objections.
iw: First HEA 1007 approval sets a template for later data center cases

t: Alabama regulators must vote publicly on big data center contracts
b: A vote is due within 90 days or the contract is deemed approved. Alabama Power must publish summaries; earlier filings redacted key terms.
iw: More scrutiny of deals

t: Duke, regulators' staff and tech giants settle on a large-load tariff
b: Would cover customers of 50 MW and up at high load factors, or 150 MW at any. Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Meta signed; it needs NCUC approval.
iw: Upfront connection costs

t: Raleigh pauses approvals for data centers over 5 MW
b: Voted 7–1; Beaufort County adopted a one-year pause the same week.
iw: Capital city pause

t: Companies tied to neighboring industrial park sue Weld County over Global AI approval
b: Three companies tied to the neighboring industrial park filed in Weld District Court on Oct. 6 (case 2026CV31187) to overturn the September approval. They allege rule-bending, open-meetings violations and unenforced stop-work orders. Responses from the county and Global AI were not found.
iw: Lawsuit could overturn a key project permit

w: Biggs (R) and Hourihan (No Labels), governor candidates
t: Biggs and Hourihan debate data centers as Hobbs skips Arizona governor debate
b: Republican Andy Biggs said the state should end tax breaks and bar new centers that crowd out residents' water and power. No Labels nominee Teri Hourihan urged a roughly six-month construction pause. Gov. Hobbs did not attend.
iw: Both challengers favor tighter limits

t: Yellowstone County sues again to test legality of new data center initiative
b: Commissioners voted 3-0 to seek a court ruling on Kassi Solberg's new initiative, which would require two-thirds voter approval before data centers start or resume operations, aimed at a May 2027 vote. The county cites the Right to Compute Act.
iw: Court ruling could block the voter-approval measure

t: Blaine County adopts 182-day emergency moratorium on data center permits
b: Commissioners voted 3-0 to stop receiving, processing and approving data center permit applications for the maximum period the law allows while staff draft zoning rules. No application had been filed.
iw: Permit applications frozen for six months

t: Republican lawmakers propose repealing Wisconsin's data center sales tax exemption
b: Sen. Andre Jacque and Reps. Sortwell, Kaufert and Brill circulated a bill to end the 2023 exemption, which the Legislative Fiscal Bureau says is worth $1.5 billion during construction and $369 million a year after. It cannot advance before January without a special session; Democratic leaders called it a stunt.
iw: Both parties now entertain ending the main state incentive

w: Interim AI and Data Center Committee
t: Interim committee hears water and local-impact testimony at Grand Farm
b: Lawmakers met near Casselton for testimony on water use, local government impacts and utilities, amid debate over Geronimo Power's proposed 540 MW Harmony Township campus. Residents asked legislators to hear township officials out; Democratic agriculture commissioner candidate Vern Thompson said the state lacks a roadmap.
iw: Study stage; no drafts advanced

t: Osawatomie data center drops tax abatement and city power commitment
b: City minutes show Alcove Development's Project Catalyst, across from Osawatomie State Hospital, grew to 283 acres while planned water use fell to 800,000 gallons a day and industrial revenue bonds, a 50 percent tax abatement and the city's power commitment were removed. No application has been filed.
iw: Incentives stripped and conditions added before any vote

t: Monticello planners recommend 547-acre hyperscale campus despite Wright County pause
b: The commission voted 4-1 to recommend the preliminary plat, rezoning and conditional use permit for Monticello Tech LLC's Edmonson Business Center. Rick Kothenbeutel opposed all three. The council has pressed Xcel on cost protections; the county's township moratorium does not apply inside the city.
iw: Hyperscale project advancing toward council vote

t: Attorney general calls FERC review of Project Jupiter gas pipeline inadequate
b: Torrez told the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission that its environmental assessment of the 17-mile Green Chile pipeline ignores Project Jupiter's own emissions and cannot justify skipping a full impact statement. He said the pipeline exists only to fuel the project.
iw: Could slow the pipeline the project depends on

t: South Elgin adopts a one-year moratorium on data center construction
b: Trustees voted unanimously after the planning and zoning commission's Sept. 16 hearing. Staff will study impacts during the year, and the board can extend it. In August the village had rejected a Dallas developer's bid to annex 20 acres for a 200,000-square-foot facility.
iw: Twelve-month construction freeze in a Kane County suburb

t: Wisconsin Rapids adopts a 12-month data center moratorium, extendable to 18
b: The pause took effect Oct. 9 and bars new proposals while the city revises its ordinance. The planning commission had voted 6-0 in August to draft it during a packed hearing on PNK Group's hyperscale proposal at the old paper mill.
iw: No new proposals accepted for at least a year

t: Hallam approves zoning for Crusoe data center at Monolith plant
b: The village board unanimously granted zoning rights for a data center that Crusoe plans at Monolith Materials' carbon black site after an hour of discussion on fire safety and noise. About half the room applauded; other residents said they felt resigned. No construction timeline has been released.
iw: Project cleared despite months of local objections

t: Moreno and Energy Secretary tout Meta-funded Perry nuclear expansion loan
b: Appearing with Energy Secretary Chris Wright to announce a federal loan for expanding the Perry nuclear plant, Moreno praised Meta for paying its own energy costs. The event came as Republicans tried to reframe the data center debate at the start of early voting.
iw: Republicans spotlight self-funded power as the model

t: Plainfield extends its data center moratorium another 180 days
b: Trustees unanimously renewed the pause on data center applications first adopted in April, which also covers warehouses used mainly for computing. Staff are writing a unified development ordinance due by early spring 2027, and the village will track state legislation. Joliet and Yorkville approved large projects this year.
iw: Pause now runs to roughly April 2027

t: Trump defends Ohio data centers at Husted rally, warns they'll go to China
b: At a Vandalia rally for Sen. Jon Husted, the president said Ohio cannot shut down data centers and his administration wants them to benefit host communities. The crowd was noticeably quieter on the topic. He praised Husted's blocked ratepayer bill.
iw: High-profile federal backing against a statewide pause

t: About 150 rally in Tonganoxie against Project Bluestem campus
b: Residents gathered to oppose Cloverleaf Infrastructure's proposed hyperscale data center and gas plant on the former Tailgate Ranch, with speakers criticizing state lawmakers over SB 98 incentives and urging voters to replace county officials in November. The county has not yet acted on the project.
iw: Sustained local opposition ahead of county decision

t: Illinois Policy says Pritzker lacked authority to halt data center tax exemption
b: The think tank's senior fellow argues the governor's pause on the sales tax exemption, announced after lawmakers rejected a pause, conflicts with a statute saying DCEO shall issue certificates to qualifying applicants. He also contends taxing business inputs is bad policy and the 2029 sunset shows legislative intent.
iw: Legal challenge framing of the incentive pause

t: Alabama's data center cost law takes effect
b: Act 2026-610 requires regulators to find that contracts for data centers of 150 MW and up cover their full cost and benefit other customers.
iw: Cost test for big contracts

t: Florida utilities file data center rates under the new state law
b: FPL says its rates already comply, with 20-year contracts and full payment for new generation. Tampa Electric filed a new tariff; Duke's is under review.
iw: Strict cost terms

t: Ellison urges PUC not to approve Xcel-Google Pine Island power deal as filed
b: In comments on docket 26-170, the AG's office said Xcel hasn't shown Google would cover all costs of the 15-year agreement, estimated other ratepayers could absorb about $1 billion, flagged stranded-cost risk and asked Xcel to justify or remove its redactions.
iw: State's consumer advocate contests the flagship supply contract

t: Loudoun campus on 342 forested acres is deferred indefinitely
b: The applicant pulled its board hearing after the planning commission unanimously recommended denial.
iw: Project stalled

t: Warner's first reelection ad focuses on data centers
b: He now says data centers need to cover their own costs, after earlier calling them a local issue.
iw: Senior Democrat turns critical

t: Judge lets the NAACP's xAI turbine case proceed
b: The Justice Department had asked the court to dismiss it. The ruling doesn't decide whether xAI broke the law.
iw: Case survives

t: Forsyth County rejects a six-month moratorium
b: Voted 5–2 after the county attorney warned of litigation, pointing to the challenge that undid Chatham County's pause.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Lee County permits a 90 MW CyrusOne data center
b: The county says the project is vested and offered no incentives.
iw: Project proceeds

t: Settlement bans data centers in most of Colleton's ACE Basin
b: Resolves a lawsuit over a 1,000 MW, 859-acre proposal. The county had adopted a six-month moratorium in July.
iw: Large area closed to data centers

t: Donalds favors local approvals with strict protections
b: His Democratic opponent, David Jolly, pledges a statewide one-year moratorium.
iw: Conditional support

t: Tazewell County moratorium on data center applications heads to the full board
b: The committee is sending the proposed pause to the county board after months of ordinance drafting. The board earlier amended its zoning code to prohibit uses not expressly listed and told staff not to accept data center petitions until the ordinance is done.
iw: Formal pause likely on top of an informal application freeze

t: McHenry County weighs a 12-month freeze on data center applications
b: The proposal would halt map and text amendments, conditional use permits, site plans, variances and building permits for data centers in unincorporated areas while staff write rules. The county draws all its water from aquifers. A committee review precedes a possible November board vote.
iw: Another collar county moving toward a pause

t: Tyrone Township drafts rules barring data centers above 60 MW
b: Officials in the Livingston County township are writing an ordinance that would prohibit facilities needing more than 60 megawatts. A moratorium blocks new applications until roughly late February or early March 2027.
iw: Size cap would exclude hyperscale projects

t: Indiana Democrats run against data center tax breaks to crack GOP supermajority
b: Mailers and ads in swing House districts say Republicans sold voters out to data centers, citing the 2019 sales tax exemption and more than $655 million in breaks. Challengers Tiffany Stoner and Ryan Kominakis aired ads against Reps. Becky Cash and Ed Soliday; Republicans say siting is a local decision.
iw: Incentive repeal becomes a legislative campaign plank

t: Sioux Falls forms oversight committee to draft data center rules
b: The council created a Regulatory Oversight Committee of four councilors to review local, state and federal rules and propose ordinances, citing the scale of the Gemini hyperscale project. Public meetings run in November, proposals are due Nov. 27, and recommendations go to the full council Jan. 12.
iw: City rules coming for the state's largest market

t: IURC approves framework for NIPSCO to buy power from its GenCo affiliate
b: Regulators approved the structure for future power purchases between NIPSCO and NiSource Generation Co., the affiliate created to build plants for data centers and other large loads, over opposition from the Office of Utility Consumer Counselor. Critics say affiliate deals weaken firewalls with the wholesale market.
iw: Eases utility-built generation for large loads despite consumer pushback

t: Coal City reviews Aligned's planned unit development for a data center campus
b: A PUD review committee has met four times since August on Aligned Data Centers' proposal for industrial park land at Reed and Carbon Hill roads, with revised comments Oct. 6 and a developer response Oct. 9. A zoning board hearing is unscheduled; the village board has the final say.
iw: Hyperscale proposal in review with no decision yet

t: Leavenworth County strips Project Bluestem critic of commission chair
b: Commissioners voted 3-2 to remove Mike Stieben, a vocal opponent of the proposed 1,000-acre Project Bluestem hyperscale campus and gas plant near Tonganoxie, from the largely ceremonial chair post. Stieben said the board is moving toward approval. More than 1,000 residents had spoken against the project at a special meeting.
iw: Board majority sidelines the project's leading opponent

t: Mesa County commissioners approve 12-month data center moratorium
b: The unanimous vote halts acceptance and approval of data center applications in unincorporated areas while the land code is rewritten. The county had no pending applications and plans to revisit in 2027.
iw: First Western Slope county pause, year-long

t: Goldwater Institute demands Pima County rescind data center moratorium
b: The think tank says the 120-day pause breaks state law, which allows moratoria only for a shortage of essential facilities or a clear and imminent danger, and raises property-rights concerns. Supervisor Allen disputes this. Draft rules go to the planning commission Oct. 28; the pause expires in January.
iw: Legal challenge could undercut the pause

t: Madison's draft data center rules would ban hyperscale facilities outright
b: The framework presented to the Plan Commission sorts data centers into small, medium and large tiers, bars anything over 100,000 square feet, requires 1,000-foot separation between medium and large sites, and confines large ones to industrial districts. A public meeting is set for Oct. 27; no ordinance is drafted yet.
iw: Permanent size cap would replace the temporary pause

t: Will County board member seeks an eight-month data center moratorium
b: Destinee Ortiz, D-Romeoville, wants the board to pause data centers in unincorporated Will County, modeled on Lake County's, while the county writes its first zoning rules and holds a public hearing. She cited water, electricity, stormwater and noise concerns from a town hall; no county projects are pending.
iw: Proposal only; no board vote scheduled

w: POWER (Protect Our Water and Energy Resources)
t: Weld County group circulates petitions for votes on Global AI data center
b: Two petitions were cleared for circulation: a referendum on commissioners' Sept. 9 approval of Global AI's Windsor project, and an initiative requiring voter approval of future data centers. Each needs 9,103 signatures. CPR reports the group is backed by a neighboring landowner.
iw: Could force a public vote on a pending project

t: Janesville unanimously adopts a 12-month pause on data center applications
b: The city stops accepting, reviewing or approving rezonings, permits, annexations and other approvals tied to data centers while it writes zoning and regulatory standards. Council Member Josh Erdman's amendment struck references to the GM/JATCO site and the November referendum so the pause covers the whole city and its extraterritorial area.
iw: Citywide freeze layered on top of the GM-site referendum

t: Rhoden touts data center law; Ahlers wants more local authority
b: In their final debate, Democrat Dan Ahlers said residents do not want data centers and local governments need more say over siting. Gov. Larry Rhoden pointed to the law he signed requiring facilities above 10 MW to cover their power and exit costs, disclose water needs and respect local bans.
iw: Both candidates accept local control; no new statewide pause

t: Toledo Blade calls statewide moratorium push political me-tooism
b: The editorial argues Amy Acton's call to attach a data center halt to the gas-tax debate is unnecessary because 138 Ohio municipalities already have moratoriums and 23 have zoning bans. It cites a BGSU poll showing 78% support for a pause but warns of lost investment.
iw: Major Ohio paper arguing against a statewide pause

t: Students rally at Illinois to demand tougher Champaign County data center rules
b: Students for Environmental Concerns led a march on the Main Quad with Prairie Rivers Network and Resist AI Data Centers Champaign County. Speakers said the county's draft ordinance lacks size and energy caps and sets renewable requirements too low, and urged pressure on legislators for the POWER Act.
iw: Organized pressure to strengthen a pending county ordinance

t: Capital Chronicle editor urges judging data centers case by case, not reflexively
b: Kelly writes that data centers and school referendums are both unpopular but should be weighed individually, suggesting residents ask whether developers pay their full share of grid upgrades beyond the state's 80% threshold, whether water needs can be met, and whether sites are industrial land rather than farmland.
iw: Centrist framing from a statewide outlet's editor

t: Pulaski County judge vetoes data center rules
b: The quorum court passed conditional-use rules 11–4; an override needs nine votes.
iw: Rules blocked for now

t: Leger Fernández calls for a pause on data centers, releases 'No Blank Checks' principles
b: Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández said AI and data centers cannot regulate themselves and urged a pause in New Mexico while communities get a say, listing standards projects should meet before approval. She spoke the day Oracle's force majeure notice on Project Jupiter was reported.
iw: Another federal Democrat backs a pause

t: Montana Supreme Court reverses itself, keeps Butte data center initiative off ballot
b: The court ordered the measure onto the November ballot Sept. 22, then vacated that order two days later because ballots had already been mailed. The initiative would require two-thirds voter approval for new data centers. Organizers asked for reconsideration.
iw: Voter-approval requirement stays off the ballot for now

t: Pritzker presses lawmakers to pass the POWER Act in the fall veto session
b: The stalled bill would make data centers cover their energy costs, bring clean generation and meet water and pollution limits. Veto session runs Nov. 17-19 and Dec. 1-3. Pritzker says new data centers should not be built without those conditions; House Republicans want a local-control bill with a three-mile buffer.
iw: Statewide pay-your-own-way rules now on a six-day session clock

t: St. Bernard adopts 12-month data center moratorium; Ivorydale plan proceeds
b: Council voted unanimously for a one-year pause, but a 24 MW, 150,000-square-foot data center proposed by CAI Investments at the former P&G Ivorydale site applied first and heads to a zoning appeals hearing Oct. 12. The developer warned the pause risks foreclosure on the property.
iw: New proposals blocked for a year in a Cincinnati suburb

t: Two-thirds of Michigan voters oppose building AI data centers
b: The Sept. 15-22 survey of 605 likely voters found 66% opposed to new AI data centers and 29% in favor. Voters trusted Democrat Abdul El-Sayed over Republican Mike Rogers on the issue 46% to 35%, wider than El-Sayed's five-point Senate lead.
iw: Deep opposition in a top Senate battleground

t: North Port adopts an 18-month data center moratorium
b: Passed 3–2, exempting a roughly 900,000-square-foot project already proposed.
iw: Long city pause

t: Arizona delegation demands answers on four data center proposals on federal land
b: Sens. Kelly and Gallego and Reps. Stanton, Ansari and Grijalva asked Interior for details on four proposals covering over 3,000 acres, part of 12 under BLM review in six states. They asked about environmental review, public input and water use.
iw: Adds scrutiny to fast-tracked federal-land projects

t: Boise mayor says no mega data center should proceed without statewide framework
b: McLean called a proposed data center on public land near Blacks Creek shortsighted and said none of that size should be considered until Idaho adopts a statewide framework. The Sierra Club also opposed the plan.
iw: Adds local political pressure against a very large project

t: Johnson and aldermen introduce a 12-month Chicago data center moratorium
b: The ordinance would pause new data center development while the city writes rules on power demand, water, emissions and noise. Co-sponsors include Alds. Hadden, Robinson and Manaa-Hoppenworth. A separate Hadden measure would make the city's 39 data centers report water and energy use. Comptroller Mendoza opposes a pause.
iw: Year-long pause proposed in Chicago, no vote scheduled yet

t: Aberdeen trucks more than a million gallons of water to Ellendale data center
b: City officials told the council that Aberdeen has sold over one million gallons in two months to Applied Digital's Ellendale, North Dakota campus, hauled across the state line about 5,000 gallons per trip. The city charges double its residential rate and says local supply is not affected.
iw: Cross-border water supply secured at a premium price

t: Ottawa ends sales contract for 300-acre data center and gas plant site
b: Commissioners voted 5-0 to terminate the city's land sale contract with Lightfield Energy after nearly two years of talks, saying the developer had not delivered a development agreement before an Oct. 30 deadline. The Proximity Park site remains for sale while a citizen ban heads to voters.
iw: Pending project loses its site

t: Woodbury enacts up-to-one-year moratorium on new and expanded data centers
b: The interim ordinance blocks rezonings, comprehensive plan amendments, conditional use permits, variances, building and electrical permits and right-of-way work for data centers, and covers any proposed water or sewer user that would rank among the city's largest. Staff said no applications are pending; three existing facilities are not covered.
iw: Broad permit freeze in a large east-metro suburb

t: State fines Vineland data center $1.07M for 62 unpermitted generators
b: DataOne must get permits within 45 days or stop running the gas generators. Regulators called it the largest enforcement action against a data center in the state.
iw: Enforcement against on-site power

t: Over 100 rally in Bow against a data center at Merrimack Station
b: Residents protested outside a select board meeting over a possible hyperscale project at the shuttered coal plant, citing water, noise and property values. No application has been filed.
iw: Organized opposition

t: New Haven adopts a 12-month data center moratorium
b: Alders present voted unanimously, with an exception for quantum computing. Without the pause, data centers would be allowed as of right in industrial zones and the Union Station area.
iw: One-year city pause

t: Wakulla County bans data centers outright
b: Unanimous, for unincorporated areas.
iw: County ban

t: Raton commission rejects data center moratorium 3-2 despite petition
b: Raton's City Commission voted 3-2 against a one-year moratorium after nearly 500 residents signed a petition. Opponents of the pause said city utilities and state oversight already provide safeguards. A feasibility deal with developer Atterix had ended in August.
iw: Pause rejected, though a regulating ordinance is still planned

t: Berthoud adopts 12-month moratorium on large data centers
b: Trustees voted 5-2 on Sept. 22 to pause applications for large data centers while the town studies water use, electricity demand and building standards. The mayor said the pause could be extended if the work is not finished.
iw: Large projects frozen for a year

t: Thornton adopts 12-month moratorium on data centers over 50,000 square feet
b: The council voted 5-3 for a year-long pause on new data centers over 50,000 square feet, after a 5-4 first-reading vote on Sept. 8. Expansions of existing large facilities are also barred. No applications were pending.
iw: Large projects frozen for a year

t: Tucson lowers large water user threshold, orders stricter proposals in 120 days
b: Council narrowly approved the first update to its 2025 ordinance, cutting the trigger for conservation plans from about 7.5 to 6.4 million gallons a month. Staff must return in 120 days with a proposal covering users above roughly 3.7 million gallons.
iw: Water-use rules tighten modestly for new large users

t: Yellowstone County asks legislators to refine Montana's Right to Compute Act
b: The three commissioners signed a letter saying the 2025 law keeps them from regulating Quantica's 5,000-acre project near Broadview. They asked local legislators to clarify counties' authority over data center land use.
iw: Local officials press for power to regulate large projects

t: De Soto approves phase one of Digital Realty's hyperscale campus
b: The planning commission approved the first-phase site plan for Project Jayhawk, a 300-acre hyperscale data center next to the Panasonic plant, with construction to start in 2027. Digital Realty has also sought a TIF district. Residents are circulating a petition to put high-impact data centers to a public vote.
iw: Second hyperscale campus advances despite a petition drive

t: Governor's data center task force holds first meeting in Grand Island
b: The 17-member panel met for more than four hours of introductory presentations on water, energy, air quality and emissions, and members took six assignments including gathering community concerns. A Lincoln County commissioner on the panel stressed keeping local control. The next meeting was set for Oct. 20 in Columbus.
iw: Study underway; recommendations due to lawmakers in 2027

t: Owen County adopts one-year data center moratorium before any proposal arrives
b: Commissioners voted unanimously for a one-year pause on new data centers and on rezonings intended for data center use, while the plan commission drafts a roughly 13-page ordinance that may cap size or acreage. Staff favored a pause over a ban in case the state limits local bans.
iw: Countywide pause plus a block on pre-emptive rezoning

t: Spartanburg County freezes data centers over 65 MW for a year
b: Passed 5–1; the Valara project already approved is unaffected.
iw: County pause with a high threshold

t: Commerce City passes six-month data center moratorium
b: The council voted 7-1 to stop accepting new data center applications while it writes rules. Officials said the city's code has no specific standards for these facilities.
iw: Applications frozen for six months

t: BLM reviews application for 4-million-square-foot Rhea Data center near Boise
b: Rhea Data, an Arevia Power subsidiary, seeks about 3,700 acres of public land in Ada County for a 600-megawatt campus with a gas plant. BLM expects to publish a notice of intent by year-end; nothing has been approved.
iw: Early federal review of a very large project with local opposition

t: Fayette County pauses data center permits through June 2027
b: After twice postponing the vote, commissioners stopped accepting zoning certificates, rezonings and building permits for new or expanded data centers in seven unincorporated townships. Already-authorized projects are exempt. The pause overlaps a comprehensive plan update due May 2027.
iw: Countywide freeze on new applications

t: Judge extends restraining order in Benton County moratorium challenge
b: After a Sept. 8 temporary restraining order, the judge kept it in place and urged developer Trent Overhue not to build until a ruling on his request for a preliminary injunction against the county's six-month pause. The county argues NSI6 LLC did not exist until three days after the moratorium.
iw: Court test of no-zoning county's power to pause

t: Zionsville pauses data centers, solar, wind and battery projects for a year
b: The council adopted a one-year moratorium covering data centers, solar and wind farms and battery storage, none of which has a land-use category in the town code. The Plan Commission will rewrite the zoning ordinance with public hearings; the town attorney cited Boone County's June pause as a prompt.
iw: Suburban Indianapolis town closed to new projects pending zoning rewrite

t: Normal extends its data center moratorium six months, to May 31, 2027
b: The council voted 6-1 to keep halting data center applications and permits while it waits for state rules; staff said local regulations should align with whatever the General Assembly passes. Council member Andy Byars dissented without comment. Mayor Chris Koos said Normal and Bloomington should mirror each other.
iw: Twin-city pause runs another six months

t: Regulators deny a Duke gas turbine, citing uncertain data center demand
b: Voted 2–1 against the 255 MW unit at Hamlet, calling its costs certain and its need uncertain.
iw: Supply buildout slowed

t: Senate Republicans back Ayotte and pledge data center legislation
b: Carson said the caucus agrees with the governor on halting data center construction and will pursue a bill to keep the costs off taxpayers. She gave no timeline.
iw: Both parties now favor a pause

t: Fauquier planners recommend denying a 900 MW Remington campus
b: The developers of the six-building project are now asking the town of Remington to annex the land.
iw: Large project in trouble

t: New Mexico Supreme Court rejects Project Jupiter challenges and lifts stays
b: The justices unanimously denied petitions from New Energy Economy and the Center for Biological Diversity and unpaused the air-permit proceeding and well use, without explanation. The Environment Department must still decide the permit.
iw: Legal setback for opponents; permitting resumes

w: Deb Haaland (D) and Gregg Hull (R), governor candidates
t: Haaland pledges day-one data center moratorium; Hull opposes
b: Democrat Deb Haaland said she would sign an executive order on her first day pausing new large-scale data centers until lawmakers pass an eight-point set of protections. Republican Gregg Hull opposes a moratorium, saying it signals New Mexico is closed for business.
iw: Possible statewide pause if Haaland wins in November

t: Clovis commission rejects 120-day data center moratorium 5-3
b: Commissioners voted 5-3 against pausing data center permits, saying no project was pending and a moratorium would signal Clovis was closed for business. Mayor Mike Morris, who proposed it, asked staff to keep drafting rules; an ordinance goes to the commission Nov. 5.
iw: Pause rejected, though zoning rules are coming

t: Colorado Springs council delays Project Taurus data center appeals to April 2027
b: Council voted 7-2 to postpone appeals of the 50-megawatt project near Garden of the Gods until April 13, 2027, citing noise and utility-rate questions. Four people were arrested at the contentious hearing.
iw: Project stalled about seven months with outcome uncertain

t: Pocatello council again affirms denial of AI data center on reconsideration
b: A motion to reverse failed 3-2, then the council affirmed the denial but waived the usual 12-month wait to reapply. The decision becomes official Oct. 1, after which Lex Developments has 28 days to seek judicial review.
iw: Denial reaffirmed, though a lawsuit is likely

t: Data center fight draws first-time candidates into Pine Island city races
b: Mayoral candidate Mark Lang and council hopeful Tosca Wohl are running on opposition to Google's hyperscale project and on transparency, against interim Mayor Brandi Veith Staloch and Council Member Delana Weis, who support it. At least three local candidates oppose the plan.
iw: Host city's leadership could flip against the project

t: St. Louis enacts size-tiered data center zoning with renewable and noise rules
b: Board Bill 49, passed unanimously Sept. 11, bars data centers from residential zones, sets setbacks up to 600 feet for facilities over 30 MW, caps noise at 5 dB over baseline, bans evaporative cooling, requires grid capacity letters, public meetings, economic impact reports and 100% renewable power by year ten.
iw: Detailed permanent rules replace an executive order

t: Massena declines to adopt a data center moratorium
b: St. Lawrence County had urged its towns to consider pauses.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Ethics Commission says Oracle disclosed $3.44 million Project Jupiter lobbying ad campaign
b: After an Ethics Commission investigation, Oracle registered and reported spending $3.44 million from January to April on ads, polling and canvassing meant to influence the Environment Department's air permit decision. The commission called it likely the largest such campaign disclosed in New Mexico.
iw: Lobbying spending now public, no penalty announced

t: Poll: nearly three-quarters of Montana voters oppose nearby data centers
b: A survey of 839 registered voters found nearly 75% oppose a data center in their city or a neighboring county, and 92% back state rules limiting effects on electricity prices. Voters split 45% to 49% on whether data centers help the economy.
iw: Broad opposition adds pressure on officials and utilities

t: Gage County replaces its eight-month pause with a 12-month moratorium
b: Supervisors adopted a new 12-month moratorium on data center permits, effective immediately and extendable, after the planning commission recommended 18 months. The county already had an eight-month pause. The board chair said it is not a ban but time to write facility-specific regulations.
iw: Permit freeze extended a full year in a county with optioned land

w: No MO Dirty Data Centers, Missouri Rural Crisis Center
t: Missouri groups stage Capitol rally as House scraps data center hearing
b: Rep. Tricia Byrnes canceled her committee's veto-day hearing on data center transparency so it would not compete with a rally organized by two opposition groups in the Capitol rotunda. Her planned People Before Powerful Interests Act would require public review of hyperscale projects.
iw: Organized statewide opposition now setting the agenda

t: Statesville and Waxhaw adopt data center pauses
b: Statesville's 180-day pause exempts the existing Compass project; Waxhaw adopted 12 months in August.
iw: Town pauses

t: Marion County pauses data centers of 50 MW or more for a year
b: Alachua County's planning commission backed a similar 12-month pause the same day.
iw: County pause

t: Lawmakers grill Entergy over charging ratepayers for Google-linked solar
b: A rider covers Cypress Solar for Google's West Memphis campus. A judge rejected Entergy's bid to stop a newspaper publishing its Google agreements.
iw: Scrutiny of cost shifting

t: Mona residents appeal Juab County permit for $10 billion data center
b: Mona Cares asked Juab County commissioners to overturn the April conditional use permit, arguing residents lacked timely notice. Commissioners said they followed state notice rules and were unsure they could cancel the permit.
iw: Administrative appeal could reopen a key permit

t: Loveland approves 12-month pause on data center land-use applications
b: Council voted 7-2 to pause land-use applications for data centers needing 10 megawatts or more; smaller facilities can still proceed. A 5-4 vote lengthened the pause from nine to 12 months, and it ends earlier if new rules are adopted.
iw: Large projects frozen for up to a year; small ones unaffected

t: Latah County adopts data center ordinance restricting groundwater cooling
b: Commissioners unanimously approved rules making data centers a conditional use in industrial zones and prohibiting consumptive groundwater use for routine cooling. No data center has been proposed in the county.
iw: Conditional approval and a groundwater cooling ban

t: Uinta County approves power-plant permit and rezoning for Prometheus data center
b: Commissioners approved a conditional use permit for on-site, off-grid power generation and rezoned a 644-acre parcel from agricultural to business industrial. The permit carries 13 conditions, including annual county inspections and road upkeep.
iw: Clears the power side of a 1.25-gigawatt campus

t: Steuben County bars data center construction for six months
b: Commissioners adopted a six-month moratorium on the plan commission's recommendation to write an ordinance governing where data centers can locate, citing limited electric and gas capacity and utility talks about new transmission lines. Proposals could still be heard only by variance.
iw: Countywide pause in northeast Indiana

t: Franklin County rezones land for two data center campuses near Pacific and Villa Ridge
b: Commissioners approved Beltline's Meramec Valley Technology Park south of Pacific, which the zoning commission had not recommended, and Provident's Gateway Digital Campus near the Shaw Nature Reserve, along with county rules on noise, construction hours, a 1,000-foot setback from homes, $20,000-a-day fines and a $10 million escrow. Residents promised lawsuits.
iw: Two campuses cleared over zoning board and resident objections

t: Edgewater enacts a permanent ban on data centers and crypto mining
b: Unanimous, ahead of a Nov. 3 vote to write it into the city charter.
iw: Permanent city ban

t: Inver Grove Heights exempts QLevr project to end moratorium lawsuit
b: Facing a Dakota County suit and an estimated exposure of at least $20 million, the council carved the 55,000-square-foot Carmen Avenue proposal out of its one-year moratorium in exchange for the developer dropping the case. The pause still applies to all other projects.
iw: Litigation pressure pried open a moratorium

t: Bemidji planning board backs one-year moratorium on data centers over 10,000 square feet
b: The board voted 6-1 to advance a one-year pause, with Mark Dickinson dissenting. Staff will draft an ordinance and hold a public forum before the City Council votes; a study during the moratorium would assess community impacts. The board had agreed in August to take the vote.
iw: Pause headed to council

t: Harvie calls for a data center moratorium in his race against Fitzpatrick
b: A new TV ad in the Bucks County House race marks a shift in his position.
iw: Pause pledge in a swing district

t: Poll: 64% of Michigan residents oppose building data centers in the state
b: A WDIV and Detroit News survey found 64.3% opposed to data center construction in Michigan, 18.9% in favor and 16.9% unsure. An MSU survey released Sept. 22 found 70% oppose one in their own community and 83% want local say over permits.
iw: Lopsided public opposition statewide

t: Business group urges scrutiny of Alliant's data center deals and gas peakers
b: The group asked the Iowa Utilities Commission and policymakers to ensure utilities don't use data center demand to justify new generation that other ratepayers pay for, pointing to Alliant's three proposed gas peaker plants and its confidential rate agreements with QTS in Cedar Rapids.
iw: Pressure on confidential utility contracts

t: Lancaster County weighs two data center task forces instead of a pause
b: Commissioners discussed creating one task force on energy and water use and another on industrial and commercial zoning for data centers. No vote was taken; the board said it is open to data centers if sited well and hopes to have a plan by year end.
iw: Study approach rather than a moratorium in the Lincoln area

t: Morton County adopts data center ordinance with three-quarter-mile home setback
b: Commissioners voted 4-1 for county rules requiring noise-producing equipment to sit at least three-quarters of a mile from occupied homes unless waived, barring tonal noise beyond property lines, and mandating closed-loop cooling. Boards may waive reclamation if a facility can be repurposed. No application is currently pending.
iw: Permanent siting and cooling standards replace a pause

t: Rapid City advances data center zoning amendments to a November vote
b: The planning commission voted 9-0 to continue Ordinance 6746 to Nov. 5 with a recommendation to approve. The amendment adds residential distance requirements, limits on power, water and sewer use, and noise and vibration standards for data centers. Council readings are set for Nov. 16 and Dec. 7.
iw: New utility and siting limits in the state's second city

t: Butternuts adopts a data center moratorium
b: Unanimous vote in Otsego County.
iw: Rural town pause

t: Weld County approves Global AI data center near Windsor, 5-0
b: Commissioners granted a Use by Special Review permit for a 41-acre campus on the former Carestream site. The first phase is 27.5 megawatts, with long-term plans up to one gigawatt. Most public comment at the daylong hearing opposed it.
iw: Approval of a large project, though petitions seek a vote

t: Montana interim committee advances draft bill to shield ratepayers from data center costs
b: The committee voted unanimously to carry the draft into the 2027 session. It would direct the PSC to set terms for customers of 5 megawatts or more and require financial guarantees. NorthWestern Energy criticized it.
iw: Likely cost-allocation and guarantee requirements in 2027

t: Environmental groups rally at Capitol for statewide data center moratorium
b: Sierra Club, Clean Water Action, Michigan Climate Action Network and the Environmental Justice Coalition held a Data Center Action Now event as the Senate returned, demanding a pause until rules exist and enforcement of conditions on the state's tax incentives.
iw: Organized pressure on lawmakers ahead of the election

t: Winona County orders study of a one-year data center moratorium
b: Commissioners unanimously directed the Planning Commission to study data centers and consider a pause of up to a year. A public hearing will follow before the board takes the issue up again; no moratorium has been adopted yet.
iw: Pause under formal study

t: Fort Wayne Journal Gazette endorses one-year data center moratorium
b: The editorial backs Councilwoman Rohli Booker's proposed pause on final approvals for large data centers while planners write standards on setbacks, noise, backup power and utility demands, plus a nine-member review commission. The council defeated the moratorium in October.
iw: Hometown paper backing a pause near Google's campus

t: Elgin council gives preliminary approval to a one-year data center moratorium
b: The committee of the whole unanimously backed the pause, which needs a final council vote. Council member Tish Powell said it could end early once an ordinance is written; Mayor David Kaptain wants to see what the state does. Elgin has no applications; South Elgin had just denied one.
iw: Kane County's largest city moving toward a pause

t: Brick introduces a ban; Bridgewater opts for rules
b: Bridgewater already doesn't permit data centers anywhere but avoided an outright ban over lawsuit concerns.
iw: More towns acting

t: Greenfield moves toward a one-year pause as more cities weigh limits
b: New Bedford is considering a ban; Northampton and Easthampton are eyeing moratoriums.
iw: More pauses likely

t: Minogue says Massachusetts can't handle more data center demand
b: Healey's Republican opponent shows little interest in new data centers either.
iw: Both candidates skeptical

t: Nottingham voters approve a 12-month data center moratorium, 1,335 to 143
b: The special election followed a warehouse-conversion proposal withdrawn amid backlash. The planning board is drafting zoning that could ban data centers permanently.
iw: One-year town pause

t: Levy and Putnam counties pause large data centers
b: Levy's moratorium runs Oct. 1 to Sept. 30, 2027, citing reliance on the Floridan Aquifer.
iw: County pauses

t: Clearfield adopts 180-day moratorium on data center development
b: The council voted 4-0 to bar data center development for six months while it studies rules, though no project is proposed. City code has no data center definition. Mayor Mark Shepherd, a MIDA board member, cited Stratos's scale.
iw: Applications frozen for six months

t: Lake County pauses data center applications in unincorporated areas until May 2027
b: The eight-month moratorium follows unanimous recommendations from the zoning board of appeals in August and the planning committee in September. The county's development ordinance does not define or regulate data centers; staff will draft rules during the pause. It is not tied to a specific project.
iw: No applications accepted in unincorporated Lake County for eight months

t: Waterloo adopts 90-day data center moratorium
b: The pause took effect immediately and blocks new projects while the council writes longer-term rules; a separate six-month pause on hyperscale projects was slated for a later vote. Residents pushed for it after the city signed an initial agreement for a 12-acre industrial site in December.
iw: Short pause with a longer hyperscale freeze pending

t: Eau Claire County starts drafting a data center moratorium for county-zoned towns
b: The Committee on Administration unanimously told corporation counsel to write a time-limited moratorium using Wisconsin Counties Association guidance. It would cover towns under county zoning such as Union, Washington, Fairchild and Seymour, not Eau Claire, Altoona or Fall Creek. Chippewa County adopted a 12-month pause in August.
iw: Another western Wisconsin county moving toward a pause

t: Kearney adopts data center zoning and approves 368 MW Tech One Crossing
b: The council voted 5-0 to create the city's first data center regulations, including a 55-decibel noise limit and conditional use permits, and granted the permit for a multi-phase campus replacing a 100 MW bitcoin mine. Full build-out would draw about 368 MW, with the first phase due in late 2027.
iw: Large campus permitted under new city rules

t: Cedar County pauses data centers, solar, wind and batteries for a year
