b: The ordinance halts larger new projects outside city limits for 12 months, extendable once by six months, citing water, power, noise, drainage and public health. Small on-site systems and existing projects are exempt. Commissioners said no project is currently proposed and called the pause due diligence.
iw: Pre-emptive countywide freeze

t: Plymouth approves one-year moratorium on data centers over 50,000 square feet
b: The council voted unanimously for the pause after a company inquired about a sizable project, choosing a 50,000-square-foot threshold over the 75,000 originally considered. It covers new proposals only; existing businesses are unaffected and no formal application had been filed.
iw: Large west-metro suburb closes to new projects

t: Attorney general backs challenges to Project Jupiter air permit hearing and emergency well
b: Torrez filed support for New Energy Economy and the Center for Biological Diversity, arguing the air-permit hearing was premature and the State Engineer misused an emergency well authorization. The Supreme Court denied both petitions on Sept. 17.
iw: Attorney general sided with opponents, but the court rejected the challenges

t: Hobbs rejects statewide data center moratorium, keeps push to end tax credit
b: Responding to the attorney general's call for a pause, the governor said data centers make sense in some places but must pay for themselves and not raise utility costs. Her office said she wants the tax credit ended permanently.
iw: Rejects a pause but wants the tax break ended

t: Senate votes 32-15 to kill ban on data center nondisclosure agreements
b: SB 2406 would have barred NDAs between government bodies and developers of data centers and other industrial projects, with penalties for companies. The committee recommended rejection, citing too little time. Gov. Armstrong testified existing transparency laws suffice. The sponsor and committee chair expect a similar bill in 2027.
iw: Transparency mandate defeated; issue returns in 2027

t: Judge throws out Edgerton's lawsuit against data center petitioners
b: Judge Stephanie Goodenow dismissed the city's suit seeking to void a 200-signature petition for a 10-year ban on hyperscale data centers. She denied an emergency order placing it on the November ballot but ordered the city to show cause at a Sept. 24 hearing why it should not appear.
iw: City loses bid to kill a citizen ban petition

t: Court says Sidney clerk illegally blocked three data center petitions
b: The justices found the city clerk wrongly refused three citizen data center petitions, which missed the Sept. 4 deadline for the November ballot and are now expected to go to a special election. It was one of four data center ballot disputes to reach the court in a month.
s: News From The States (Ohio Capital Journal)
iw: Clears path for a local ban vote in Shelby County

t: Knox County's Liberty Township resolves to prohibit data centers
b: Trustees passed a resolution explicitly barring data centers, with a trustee saying unregulated facilities should not be permitted. At least three other Knox County townships have proposed bans, and the Logan-Union-Champaign planning commission has reviewed 28 nearly identical township definitions that effectively prohibit data centers since April.
s: News From The States (Ohio Capital Journal)
iw: Township-level bans multiplying across rural central Ohio

t: Toledo Blade backs Trump's defense of data centers against local opposition
b: The editorial endorses the president's Truth Social post urging communities to welcome data centers, citing Blade reporting that the industry accounts for $10.5 billion of $11 billion in new northwest Ohio projects. It notes Rep. Bob Latta's request for an FBI probe of Chinese social media influence.
iw: Pro-development editorial tied to presidential intervention

t: House Democrats plan a 24-month moratorium bill for 2027
b: Announced the same day Ayotte said she opposes any data center in the state.
iw: Bipartisan appetite for a pause

t: Journal poll: 65% of New Mexico voters oppose large data centers
b: An Aug. 21-28 poll of 516 likely voters found 65% oppose building large data centers and 75% support a statewide moratorium until rules are set. Opposition was higher among Democrats but a majority of Republicans also opposed.
iw: Broad bipartisan opposition adds political pressure

t: House refuses to take up data center permitting moratorium in special session
b: A Democratic motion to introduce a bill pausing data center permitting through June 2027 failed 68-25 on the special session's first day. In the Senate, David Hogue objected to a similar bill and no override motion was made. Legislative Management had declined to advance the moratorium on Aug. 17.
iw: Statewide pause blocked in both chambers

t: Bulloch County rejects an outright ban 4–3 but keeps its pause
b: The moratorium runs through Dec. 31 while the county writes regulations.
iw: Pause continues

t: Mattoon halts new data centers over half an acre until the council lifts it
b: The moratorium covers facilities larger than 21,780 square feet inside the city and 1.5 miles beyond, renews annually and has no fixed end date. Council cited water, power costs, health and city finances. Existing businesses that meet the definition may keep operating.
iw: Open-ended pause with no sunset

t: South Dakota PUC candidates split over one-year AI data center pause
b: Democrat Frank Kloucek, running for the open Public Utilities Commission seat, backs a one-year moratorium on new AI data centers and says this year's laws lack enforcement teeth. Republican Don Haggar calls the idea reckless and says the new framework lets regulators judge each case on its merits.
iw: Regulator race turns on whether to pause

t: SLU professor says Missouri's data center push needs transparency and enforcement
b: The Missouri Independent commentary contrasts St. Charles's effective ban, St. Charles County's six-month moratorium and St. Louis's conditional approval, questions permanent job counts at Meta's Kansas City site and the Liberty project, and credits the House Future Caucus framework while saying NDAs eroded trust.
iw: Academic voice centering disclosure in Missouri debate

t: Springhill Township bars new data center and power plant applications
b: A temporary ban while it writes setback and noise rules, prompted by interest in 800 acres near Gans.
iw: Temporary township ban

t: Lamont: Connecticut is the wrong place for massive AI data centers
b: He'd consider projects that bring their own power, pass utility regulators and win local approval. Earlier he urged the state to slow down new data centers.
iw: Governor discourages hyperscale projects

t: Fazio wants to end Connecticut's data center tax breaks
b: The Republican nominee opposes incentives but not an outright ban.
iw: Both candidates cool on incentives

t: Gorham moves toward a permanent data center ban
b: Councilors unanimously sent the proposal to the planning board; a temporary moratorium is already in place.
iw: Possible permanent ban

t: Hopkinton imposes a 60-day emergency pause
b: Unanimous, while the planning board drafts a permanent zoning amendment.
iw: Short emergency pause

t: Christiansburg ends by-right data centers
b: Voted 6–0 to require conditional use permits in industrial zones.
iw: Slower approvals

t: Data Center Fair Share Act would tie highway funds to data center tariffs
b: States would need tariffs making data centers cover their own energy infrastructure.
iw: Federal cost pressure

t: Southaven approves another SpaceXAI data center
b: The company's fifth in the Memphis area.
iw: Project approved

t: Indiantown and Taylor County reject data center pauses
b: Indiantown's council voted 4–1 and fired its village manager the same night.
iw: Pauses rejected

t: Aurora council finalizes ban on evaporative cooling in new buildings, including data centers
b: The council introduced the ordinance unanimously Sept. 14, and Denver7 reports the ban passed at the next meeting. It covers new commercial, industrial and multifamily buildings and is not retroactive, so Aurora's nine existing data centers are unaffected. The effective date is unconfirmed.
iw: Forces closed-loop cooling on new projects

t: Magellan poll: most Colorado voters oppose data centers, strongest near home
b: A survey of 1,389 registered voters found 86% oppose one near their neighborhood, 82% in their city or town and 75% elsewhere in the state. Fifty-five percent chose a ban on construction as the best path for their community.
iw: Broad opposition adds pressure on local officials

w: Alani Bankhead (D) and Seth Bodnar (I), Senate candidates
t: Montana Senate candidates Bankhead and Bodnar lay out data center positions
b: Democrat Alani Bankhead called for a moratorium on large data center development until community impacts are studied. Independent Seth Bodnar pledged to shield ratepayers and give communities the final say. The candidates agreed projects need more transparency.
iw: Moratorium and community-veto pledges in an open Senate race

t: Natrona County weighs conditions and industrial-park zoning for Prometheus data center
b: At a packed September meeting, commissioners heard Prometheus Hyperscale's plan for a roughly 1.25-gigawatt campus east of Casper. They are drafting conditions and weighing an industrial-park exemption that would bypass the state Industrial Siting Council.
iw: Zoning path and conditions still undecided

t: Marquette poll: 74% say data center costs outweigh benefits, 68% back a pause
b: Opposition spans parties, at 57% of Republicans, 83% of independents and 90% of Democrats, up from a roughly even split in 2025. Support for a one-year construction moratorium holds near 68%. Only about 5% call data centers their top issue, well behind cost of living and immigration.
iw: Broad bipartisan opposition, though low election salience

t: BGSU poll: 78% of Ohio voters back a temporary data center ban
b: A Sept. 1–10 YouGov survey of 1,000 likely voters found 75% oppose a data center in their community and 63% oppose them statewide. Majorities say the facilities hurt the environment, energy costs and quality of life, all up since April. Acton and Brown each led 48–45.
s: BGSU Democracy and Public Policy Research Network
iw: Broad public support for a pause raises political risk

t: Warren adopts 12-month data center moratorium
b: Council in Michigan's third-largest city voted unanimously for a one-year pause, citing concerns that large facilities would strain local electrical infrastructure.
iw: Year-long freeze in a major Detroit suburb

t: Dearborn gives final approval to six-month data center moratorium
b: Council finalized a six-month pause on data center construction, following a first reading earlier in September, to give the city time to write regulations.
iw: Another Detroit-area city halts new projects

t: Port Huron Township approves 12-month pause on high-demand facilities
b: The township board adopted a one-year moratorium on data centers and other high resource-demand facilities, extendable if more time is needed to write rules. Brighton Township in Livingston County adopted its own pause the same week while its planning commission drafts an ordinance.
iw: New freezes in St. Clair and Livingston counties

t: Farmington neighbors drop lawsuit against Tract's golf-course data center
b: The nonprofit formed by residents withdrew its suit after running out of money, clearing the way for construction on the former golf course that the council approved 4-1 in late 2024. Neighbors cite noise, lighting and falling home values; one couple plans to sell.
iw: Legal challenge collapsed, construction proceeds

t: Masterson defends the incentive law and says locals should decide siting
b: The Republican nominee for governor stands by his vote for SB 98, calls it one of the most restrictive data center laws, and says cities and counties should make siting decisions. His ratepayer pledge has developers pay power costs, opposes eminent domain and protects water. He accused Holscher of flip-flopping.
iw: Frontrunner opposes a statewide pause, favors local control

t: Husted's Ratepayer Protection Act passes House, blocked by Senate Democrats
b: The bill, which would encourage states to make data center developers cover added electricity infrastructure costs, passed the U.S. House in mid-September. Senate Democrats blocked it before the election recess, calling its voluntary standards toothless. Husted says siting should stay local; Brown calls him the face of data centers.
iw: Federal cost-shifting bill stalls amid Senate race fight

t: Warren County directs prosecutor to draft a data center moratorium
b: Commissioners asked the prosecutor's office to draft a temporary moratorium after noting the county's rural zoning code has no definitions or rules for hyperscale facilities. A vote on the draft had not been scheduled.
s: Data Centers Weekly Briefing (citing Warren County Post)
iw: Another Cincinnati-area county moving toward a pause

t: Mead trustees approve 12-month data center moratorium on a 4-2 vote
b: The pause prevents data center applications while staff study infrastructure, water use and setbacks. The town attorney said it does not permanently prohibit data centers. The two dissenting trustees questioned whether a full year was needed.
iw: Applications frozen for up to a year

t: Attorney General Mayes calls for statewide pause on new data center approvals
b: Citing rising energy bills and a nearly 30% cut to Colorado River supplies, Mayes urged lawmakers and the governor to halt approvals, especially hyperscale AI projects, until the state has a plan. She does not have power to impose one.
iw: First statewide official to call for a pause

t: Switzerland County passes one-year data center moratorium
b: Commissioners approved the pause at a special meeting. Vermillion County created a committee Aug. 25 to draft ordinance language after scrapping an earlier version, while Jefferson County's plan commission declined Sept. 1 to pursue a moratorium. About 25 Indiana counties now have pauses.
iw: Ohio River county closes to new projects

t: Barber County approves agreement for Google's first Kansas data center
b: Commissioners gave final approval 2-0-1 to a development agreement for Project Helium, a 1.7 million square foot air-cooled campus near Sharon. Google may not drill new wells and must meet noise limits. Construction is expected in early 2027; the county projects nearly $10 million a year in property tax.
iw: Hyperscale project cleared with negotiated water and noise terms

w: Interim AI and Data Center Committee
t: North Dakota interim committee reviews data center growth, water and zoning
b: The Legislature's Artificial Intelligence and Data Center Committee heard from the PSC chair, the counties association and researchers on grid effects, permitting timelines and local zoning authority. Public comment focused on water use and nondisclosure agreements. No bill drafts were advanced; the next meeting was set for Oct. 6.
iw: Study only; possible 2027 legislation on zoning and disclosure

t: Ohio Capital Journal columnist says state leaders courted data centers without public input
b: The column argues Ohio politicians welcomed hundreds of facilities while residents absorb higher bills, grid strain, water use and noise for few permanent jobs. It cites $2.3 billion in sales tax exemptions, the Perkins and Oxford Township fights, and Conserve Ohio's ballot amendment effort.
iw: Statewide commentary framing backlash as a leadership failure

t: Data centers must report water and energy use every six months
b: S3379 also came with state guidance for towns negotiating community benefits agreements. Advocates called it too weak and renewed calls for a moratorium.
iw: New disclosure duties

t: Self-powered Spartanburg data center isn't subject to power plant rules
b: The ruling covers the $2.8 billion project at a former Kohler plant.
iw: Lighter rules for self-power

t: Tallahassee rejects an AI data center ban 3–2
b: Commissioners said existing zoning already excludes such facilities.
iw: Ban rejected, zoning already restrictive

w: Skull Valley Band of Goshute Indians
t: Skull Valley Goshute tribe opposes data center plans in Tooele County
b: The tribe said a hyperscale data center in Tooele County could harm the groundwater that is its sole water source. KSL tied the statement to the Army's Dugway proposal; the tribe urged county officials to oppose related zoning requests.
iw: Adds tribal water-rights opposition

w: Phil Weiser (D) and Greg Lopez (I), governor candidates
t: Colorado governor candidates split on state data center rules at debate
b: Democrat Phil Weiser backed a state law protecting community interests, clean energy standards and utility rates. Independent Greg Lopez said the jury is still out and cited water worries. Republican Victor Marx skipped the debate.
iw: Possible state regulation after the November election

w: Wyoming Minerals, Business and Economic Dev. Committee
t: Wyoming committee narrowly kills draft exempting some power generators from utility rules
b: After carrying the draft forward in June, the Minerals committee voted it down Aug. 27 as four House members opposed it. It would have let producers serving a 25-megawatt customer operate outside utility rules. Senator Rothfuss's Blockchain committee is weighing a rival version.
iw: Off-grid power exemption stalled, though rival bills continue

t: Nehawka bans data centers and crypto mining in its zoning jurisdiction
b: The Cass County village board adopted an ordinance prohibiting data centers, crypto mining, blockchain computing and the power plants that would run them within its zoning jurisdiction, effective in 15 days. The county's own moratorium had not covered the village's extraterritorial area.
iw: Outright ban closes a gap in the county pause

t: Lancaster County weighs 12-month data center moratorium outside cities
b: Commissioners discussed but did not pass a resolution pausing construction, building permits and conditional use permits for data centers in unincorporated areas for up to a year while a study committee writes zoning rules. The pause would not reach Hallam. The board revised the draft for a later meeting.
iw: Pause considered for the Lincoln area, later swapped for task forces

t: Judge weighs dismissing Sunshine suit over Montgomery County Amazon approvals
b: Judge Cotton Walker heard argument on the state and county's motion to dismiss Preserve Montgomery County's February lawsuit, which says officials failed to post proper notice and disclose water, power and abatement terms for the Amazon campus. He took it under advisement with another hearing set for Sept. 4.
iw: Transparency challenge to a $10 billion project still alive

t: Elkhart stops data center and battery storage applications through 2027
b: At a special meeting the council voted 9–0 to stop accepting applications for data centers and battery energy storage facilities through Dec. 31, 2027. The pause applies only inside city limits. Members said it buys time to study effects on the local labor pool and infrastructure.
iw: Sixteen-month freeze on new applications in a northern Indiana city

t: Pinal County rejects Vermaland's La Osa data center near Eloy, 4-1
b: Supervisors denied rezoning for what would have been Arizona's largest data center, on about 3,300 acres. The developer had cut the plan from 59 buildings to 11. Residents raised water, power, noise and wildlife concerns.
iw: Largest proposed Arizona campus killed by rezoning vote

t: Bloomington and Normal hold a joint data center forum while both pause hyperscale projects
b: The two governments convened a three-hour panel with the Citizens Utility Board, Prairie Rivers Network, the Data Center Coalition and others to answer residents' questions on environment, land use, infrastructure and economics. Both communities have moratoriums on hyperscale data centers while they draft regulations; each will run its own review.
iw: Twin-city pauses confirmed by an official source; rules still pending

t: Orangetown pauses data centers and battery storage for six months
b: Residents objected that the pause doesn't reach DataBank's proposed second facility, already under environmental review near Lake Tappan.
iw: Pause, but the pending project is exempt

t: Two Bessemer council members who backed Project Marvel lose their seats
b: A third was forced into a runoff and the mayor, who signed an NDA, faces one too.
iw: Voters punish approvals

t: Durham County pauses large data centers through May 2027
b: Voted 4–1, aligning with the city; small closed-loop projects without diesel generators are exempt.
iw: Nine-month pause

t: Rep. Vasquez co-sponsors two federal data center transparency bills
b: Rep. Gabe Vasquez joined the FAIR Data Act, shielding residential and small-business customers from data center energy costs, and the Data Center Water and Energy Transparency Act, which would require usage disclosure with fines up to $20,000 a day.
iw: Backs cost-protection and disclosure mandates

t: Colfax County adopts one-year moratorium on data centers
b: Commissioners unanimously adopted Ordinance 2026-02, a one-year moratorium on data centers in unincorporated areas, citing drought and water, energy, heat and noise concerns. It does not cover Raton or other municipalities. Exact vote date needs confirming.
iw: Applications frozen for a year in unincorporated areas

t: Montana energy task force urges clear path for large loads without cost shifts
b: The 20-recommendation final report asks the state to intervene in NorthWestern's large-load tariff case and clarify how utilities serve loads like data centers, with no rate impacts or stranded costs for existing customers. Its first item is considering an appointed PSC.
iw: Wants faster service for large loads but protected ratepayers

t: Mackinac Center calls Michigan data center bills mostly bad, concerns overblown
b: The free-market think tank's commentary says water and power worries are exaggerated and criticizes three kinds of proposals: moratoriums such as SB 1018, special rules for data centers, and labor provisions in HBs 5777, 5786 and 5787. It urges equal treatment and no incentives.
iw: Think tank opposing both restrictions and subsidies

t: Stansbury demands public accounting of Project Jupiter's water sources
b: Rep. Melanie Stansbury asked the attorney general, state engineer, environment secretary and Interstate Stream Commission for water-use, water-rights and compact-compliance details, calling for an inquiry into long-term use. She said the project's own estimates have shifted.
iw: Adds federal scrutiny of the project's water supply

t: Minnehaha County unveils first draft of a data center ordinance
b: Planning staff and commissioners presented an initial data center ordinance to the planning commission and residents. The county will redraft it before a formal hearing on the text amendment; no dates were set. One speaker urged ownership requirements tied to South Dakota residency.
iw: New county rules coming for the Sioux Falls area

t: Mandan planners recommend data center ordinance with noise and coolant limits
b: The commission unanimously recommended a city data center ordinance with six amendments, including tighter noise limits, added monitoring and a requirement for PFAS-free coolants, sending it to the City Commission. Stark Power is proposing a gas-powered data center campus near Mandan schools and plans to apply after rules are final.
iw: New conditions ahead of a pending gas-powered campus

t: Carlton County adopts one-year pause on new or expanded data centers
b: Interim Ordinance 42 halts creation or expansion of data centers countywide under Minn. Stat. 394.34 while the county studies impacts, considers changes to its official controls and finishes the comprehensive land use plan begun in 2025. The board had advanced the ordinance in July after community pushback.
s: Blandin on Broadband (Moose Lake Star Gazette)
iw: County next to the Hermantown project freezes

t: New Mexico Supreme Court pauses Project Jupiter air permit hearing and emergency well use
b: Two unanimous orders halted the Sept. 14 air-quality permit hearing and paused an emergency well authorization, after petitions from two environmental groups. The court denied both petitions and lifted both stays on Sept. 17.
iw: Stays were temporary; permitting and well use resumed Sept. 17

t: Regulators order Rhode Island Energy to propose a tariff for 20 MW-plus loads
b: The rate case ruling requires a filing by Dec. 31 meant to keep data centers and other very large loads from shifting costs, straining reliability or causing rate shock. Legislative cost bills had stalled.
iw: Cost protections coming

t: Cox calls for MIDA overhaul and bigger governor role after Stratos backlash
b: Gov. Cox called for changes to the agency that approved Stratos, including a larger role for his office. MIDA said it had paused work on Stratos during litigation, while developer Kevin O'Leary said the project is full steam ahead.
iw: Signals tighter oversight of fast-track approvals

t: Hualapai Tribe moves to bar hyperscale data centers on its reservation
b: The council passed a resolution opposing hyperscale data centers, which KJZZ describes as a moratorium. It cites Colorado River shortages and says no developer may use tribal resources without the tribe's free, prior and informed consent.
iw: Closes a large reservation, but no project was proposed

t: Republican Senate nominee Rogers backs a one-year statewide data center pause
b: Rogers told the Detroit News he supports a state-approved one-year moratorium on new data centers, not a federal ban, and a transparent process putting local communities first. The shift from his earlier pro-buildout stance drew skepticism from Democrat Abdul El-Sayed.
iw: Both Senate nominees now favor limits

t: McDonough County votes down a one-year data center moratorium 13-7
b: The resolution from board member Ken Durkin had cleared the Law and Legal Committee 6-1. Opponents said it was not legally binding, would signal the county is closed to developers and would limit property owners. Supporters wanted time to study impacts.
iw: Proposed pause rejected; county stays open to proposals

t: Indianapolis approves $85 million in abatements for Sabey campus alongside pause
b: At the meeting that ratified the city's moratorium, the commission granted Sabey Data Center Properties a 10-year real property abatement worth about $49.5 million and a 15-year personal property abatement worth about $36 million for its $2 billion Decatur Township campus, expected to create 75 jobs.
iw: Large incentive package for an exempted project

t: House challenger demands southern Minnesota data center moratorium
b: Ahead of Google's Pine Island celebration, the 1st District Democrat said projects should stop unless they lower bills, protect farmland and water, deliver local gains and end NDAs. Incumbent Rep. Brad Finstad says communities should decide and companies should be transparent.
iw: Moratorium call in a congressional race

t: Greensboro pauses data centers over 10 MW for 180 days
b: Voted 8–0; runs through Feb. 14, 2027.
iw: City pause

t: Wyoming primary: Barlow wins governor nomination, moratorium backer Bien loses
b: State Sen. Eric Barlow, who says communities should decide on data center proposals, won the Republican nomination. Brent Bien, who promised a moratorium, lost. WyoFile found no sign that anti-data-center positions won local races in the southeast.
iw: A statewide pause pledge failed to win the nomination

t: Oneida County adopts a one-year data center moratorium with no project in sight
b: The unanimous vote stops the county from accepting or approving permits for new data centers in zoned areas, excluding Rhinelander and three unzoned towns, while it writes rules likely limiting them to certain districts. The chair said the county would otherwise be open season for developers.
iw: Pre-emptive pause across a Northwoods county

t: Freeborn County extends data center moratorium to August 2027
b: Commissioners renewed the year-old ban on accepting or approving data center permits in unincorporated areas while staff write regulations, saying current rules don't address the facilities' impacts and letting the pause lapse could threaten orderly development.
iw: Second year of a full permit freeze

t: Pillen names 17 members to the Data Center Task Force
b: Appointees include the heads of Berkshire Hathaway Energy, OPPD, NPPD and the Greater Omaha Chamber, a Public Service commissioner and Lancaster and Sarpy county commissioners. The group, overseen by the water and energy department, will study grid, water and infrastructure impacts and draft county zoning guidance, meeting first in September.
iw: Industry-heavy study panel; no new restrictions yet

t: Pine County stretches data center moratorium from six to twelve months
b: After a public hearing, the board unanimously replaced its July 7 six-month interim ordinance with a 12-month pause effective Aug. 18 so a work group can draft regulations. The county has received no data center inquiries; residents raised light, noise, water, ecological and transparency concerns.
iw: Pause doubled with no project in sight

t: Ottawa extends its data center moratorium a year, through Aug. 25, 2027
b: The unanimous vote lengthens a six-month pause adopted in March that covers all zoning districts. Mayor Robert Hasty said the city is drafting its own ordinance but wants to align it with whatever the state passes after the POWER Act stalled in spring. No project is pending.
iw: LaSalle County seat closed to data centers for another year

t: Alamance County adopts a one-year pause on 10 MW projects
b: Unanimous, after it grew from a six-month proposal.
iw: County pause

t: Madison County adopts a three-year moratorium
b: Voted 8–0; Union and Carroll counties adopted one-year pauses in June and Russellville six months in July.
iw: Long pause

w: Third Judicial District Court (Judge James Kaste)
t: Judge dismisses residents' challenge to Uinta County permits for Prometheus data center
b: Three residents alleged unadvertised meetings and undisclosed family ties between officials and the developer. The judge dismissed the petition because they missed a response deadline and did not show personal harm. One petitioner had dropped out earlier.
iw: Legal challenge to the county permits ended

t: Bailey wants an immediate halt to all data center tax breaks, including existing ones
b: The Republican nominee for governor now claims credit for Pritzker's incentive pause and says he would go further by suspending existing agreements, require data centers to supply their own power, roll back the state climate law and have them fund utility relief. Pritzker frames his approach as responsible growth.
iw: Both governor candidates now run against incentives

t: South Elgin rejects annexation for a 200,000-square-foot data center
b: The board unanimously turned down White Rose Partners' request to annex 20 acres at Route 25 and Kenyon Road for the project. The vote preceded a village-wide moratorium adopted in October.
iw: Specific project turned away at the annexation stage

t: Husted says data center industry has earned the backlash
b: In a Statehouse News Bureau interview, the Republican senator faulted companies for not offering to cover energy bills in communities that host power plants, while pointing to his Ratepayer Protection Act and saying further decisions belong to local officials.
iw: Industry's chief Republican ally distances himself

t: Dubuque orders up six-month moratorium after survey shows 76% opposed
b: Mayor Brad Cavanagh directed the city attorney to draft a six-month pause for a Sept. 8 vote after 3,777 survey responses showed 76% against large data centers. Developer Karis has eyed 420 acres of farmland east of the airport. A draft ordinance is targeted for November.
iw: City pause drafted amid strong public opposition

t: Toledo Blade faults developers for sneaking projects through emergency ordinances
b: After the Ohio Supreme Court struck Ashville's emergency resolution for an EdgeConneX hyperscale campus and gas plant, blocking a referendum attempt, the editorial says developers are losing public support through behind-the-scenes maneuvers and should make their case in public.
iw: Pro-industry paper warning the industry on transparency

t: Colorado Springs mayor sets 'community-first' standards for data centers
b: The city page says data centers will not be approved by default. Large projects must pay for new electric infrastructure and reserved capacity, show water availability, limit neighborhood impacts, and keep public hearings. It is a policy statement, not an ordinance.
iw: Higher bar for approval and cost responsibility

t: Spanberger rules out a statewide data center moratorium
b: She called local pauses a local choice and pointed to her cost rules instead.
iw: No state pause

t: Rock County committee unanimously rejects a countywide data center moratorium
b: The Planning and Development Committee killed a 12-month moratorium resolution from Supervisors Doug Sutter and Kim Schneider after counsel said a 1970s resolution ceded zoning to the towns, leaving the county no authority and exposing it to developer lawsuits. A proposed 13-member study panel also failed and will be revised.
iw: No county-level pause, though several towns have their own

t: Regulators vote 3–1 to keep Meta's data center details secret
b: Overturned a judge's subpoena for how Meta calculated its jobs and power needs. The vote split along party lines.
iw: Less disclosure

t: Leavenworth County lets moratorium lapse but sends data center rules back
b: The county's 90-day moratorium, passed 3-2 in May amid the 1,000-acre Project Bluestem proposal near Tonganoxie, expired after commissioners declined to extend it. The planning commission then voted 8-1 to rework draft regulations rather than adopt them, after about 100 residents sought stricter noise and water limits.
iw: Pause ended, but rules sent back for a stricter rewrite

t: Spotsylvania backs a call for a statewide moratorium
b: Supervisors voted 4–2 to support Sen. Glen Sturtevant's request to the governor. Eight data centers are in the works in the county.
iw: Local pressure for a state pause

w: Interim Science, Technology and Telecom Committee
t: Interim committee hears first pitch for statewide data center moratorium
b: Reps. Micaela Lara Cadena and Angelica Rubio told the interim committee in Socorro they will introduce a statewide moratorium in January, with its definition and length still open. Republican members urged a study of job and economic effects first.
iw: Statewide pause gets its first hearing, with GOP resistance

t: Douglas County approves $19.3 million tax rebate for Parker data center
b: Commissioners voted unanimously to rebate the county's share of business personal property tax for a 22.5-megawatt Flexential facility over 35 years. Every public commenter opposed it. The company says it will create 16 jobs.
iw: Long county tax break in a state with no state incentive

t: Judge rules Yellowstone County data center initiative missed signature deadline
b: The judge held the deadline passed July 13, not Aug. 12 as organizers were first told, so the voter-approval measure stays off the November ballot. Organizers had gathered roughly 15,000 signatures against about 16,600 needed.
iw: Voter-approval measure blocked for Quantica's Broadview project

t: Chicago executive order adds environmental review for data centers, seeks a pause
b: Executive Order 2026-5 gives the city 90 days to write air-permit and noise rules for backup generators and cooling, requires four departments to review any development with a data center within 60 days, and creates a task force due March 15, 2027. It asks the council for a time-limited moratorium.
iw: New permit conditions and review steps in the state's biggest market

t: Cass County votes 5-0 for a 12-month data center moratorium
b: Commissioners unanimously paused data center permits for a year and tabled proposed regulations until Sept. 22. Tenaska has optioned farmland near Plattsmouth; residents cited water, electricity and farmland loss, while supporters pointed to tax revenue. The county pause did not cover villages' zoning jurisdictions.
iw: Year-long freeze where a developer holds land options

t: Democrats propose data center NDA ban and temporary moratorium for special session
b: Sen. Tim Mathern and Vern Thompson, the Democratic nominee for agriculture commissioner, called for a ban on nondisclosure agreements between officials and developers and a temporary halt on data center development ahead of the September special session. Senate Majority Leader David Hogue said the interim committee was the proper venue.
iw: Moratorium enters statewide campaign debate

t: Nance County halts data center permits for up to a year
b: Supervisors adopted Resolution 26-13, effective immediately, barring construction starts, building permits and conditional use permits for data centers for up to 12 months or until the county adopts new zoning rules addressing infrastructure and environmental concerns.
iw: Another rural county permit freeze

t: House Future Caucus issues local data center guidance, plans 2027 cost bill
b: Rep. Collin Willenkamp said his AI Infrastructure, Grid Integrity and Water Resources Protection Act will return in 2027, requiring large loads to pay for grid expansion and creating a rate class. The caucus released questions for communities on decommissioning, renewables and ratepayer protection, and did not back a special session.
iw: Cost-allocation bill queued for next session

t: GOP lawmaker proposes guardrails for embracing data centers in Michigan
b: The Rochester Hills Republican's Bridge Michigan commentary argues data centers are a form of manufacturing Michigan should welcome, with rules favoring former industrial sites, returning water to its watershed, closed-loop cooling for groundwater users, self-supplied power off the public grid, and existing noise and lighting standards.
iw: Legislator sketching a pro-development regulatory framework

t: Nichols column says data centers are becoming a defining 2026 election issue
b: The Cap Times associate editor argues opposition to AI data centers now cuts across party lines, citing Rebecca Cooke's ad against Derrick Van Orden and moratorium pledge, Emily Berge's federal pause call, Francesca Hong's early support, Kansas nominee Cindy Holscher's primary win and Abdul El-Sayed's public-ownership proposal.
iw: Progressive columnist framing moratorium candidates as a trend

t: Building trades leader says community benefits, not moratoriums, should guide Indiana
b: The Indiana State Building and Construction Trades Council director argues in the Indiana Capital Chronicle that blanket pauses deter responsible developers, and that local leaders should instead negotiate concrete terms, citing Microsoft's school-tax deal in LaPorte and Amazon's infrastructure funding in Hobart.
iw: Labor voice against local moratoriums

t: Judge blocks four new diesel generators at Lowell's data center
b: Residents challenged the state's air permit for eight more generators; four already installed can keep running.
iw: Court limits backup power expansion

t: Independence County adopts a five-year moratorium
b: Runs through Aug. 31, 2031, citing water supply strain; no project had been proposed.
iw: Very long pause

t: Aurora council rejects six-month data center moratorium on a 6-5 tiebreak
b: The mayor broke a tie against the pause. Council instead directed the city manager to draft standards within 35 days, including a possible ban on evaporative cooling and buffer zones near neighborhoods.
iw: Pause rejected, though new standards are coming

t: Benton County adopts six-month data center moratorium, drawing developer lawsuit
b: Commissioners signed the pause as developer Trent Overhue prepared to buy 12 acres on Highway 65 near Warsaw for two 20,000-square-foot buildings. Overhue and NSI6 LLC sued, arguing he chose the county because it has no planning and zoning. The county says the pause exempts only projects already under construction.
iw: Pause lands on a project days from closing

t: Beshear order bars passing data center costs to other ratepayers
b: Executive Order 2026-494 also lets agencies deny permits on water and air grounds and expects full tax payment. Local approval is still up to communities.
iw: New cost and permit conditions

t: PSC resets review of $1.3-1.7 billion transmission plan for Port Washington campus
b: Commissioners unanimously revoked the completeness finding for American Transmission Co.'s Ozaukee County project after 564 refiled documents, closing the docket and ending a December deadline. ATC must reapply, likely delaying lines serving the Vantage, Oracle and OpenAI campus. ATC had hoped to build from December 2026.
iw: Grid connection for the state's largest campus pushed back

t: Nessel asks appeals court to void DTE's Saline data center contracts
b: Her brief argues the Public Service Commission acted arbitrarily and unlawfully by approving DTE's heavily redacted contracts for the 1.4 GW Saline Township campus without a contested hearing, ignored its own standards and omitted transmission costs. She wants the approval vacated and remanded.
iw: Legal cloud over the state's largest approved project

t: Vineland weighs a revised 300 MW self-powered AI campus
b: The DataOne/Nebius plan would generate its own power; residents raised LNG storage, emissions, water and noise concerns.
iw: Large project still under review

t: Tucson adopts first data center rules, requiring rezoning and half-mile buffers
b: The 6-1 vote covers facilities over 25,000 square feet or 20 megawatts. They need council-approved rezoning, no potable water for cooling, and a half-mile buffer from homes and schools. Staff will study a possible ban. Effective Sept. 4.
iw: Council discretion and large buffers raise hurdles

t: Gilbert planning commission backs strict data center rules; council vote pending
b: The recommendation would limit data centers to industrial zones, require a 650-foot setback from homes, and ban drinking water and open-loop evaporative cooling. Council held a study session in August and the vote slipped from September; reports differ on whether it is now Nov. 12 or December.
iw: Large setback and potable-water ban if adopted

t: PUCO makes data centers give AEP Ohio 180 days' notice before default service
b: Regulators ordered that data centers returning to AEP Ohio's standard service offer give six months' notice, after which the utility buys their power through separate auctions or spot purchases and assigns the full cost to the data center, shielding other customers.
iw: Adds cost exposure and lead time for large loads switching supply

t: Sanpete County approves six-month data center moratorium
b: Commissioners approved a six-month moratorium on new data center development at their Aug. 4 meeting, giving the county time to draft land-use rules. The county had no ordinance covering data centers; planners began discussing rules in May.
iw: New applications frozen for six months

t: Coeur d'Alene council opposes approving data centers until study is complete
b: Council unanimously adopted Resolution 26-065 opposing construction, expansion or approval of data centers within city limits until further analysis and policy review. Proposals would still receive due process. No data centers operate in the city.
iw: Signals denial of near-term approvals in the city

t: Jackson County replaces expiring pause with broader one-year moratorium
b: The unanimous ordinance halts high-density computing and data-processing facilities in unincorporated areas through Aug. 4, 2027, superseding a pause set to end Aug. 31. Officials are still reviewing noise, water, generator and decommissioning rules before the zoning commission recommends an ordinance.
iw: Pause extended and widened

t: Sand proposes ending Iowa data center tax breaks and banning NDAs
b: The Democrat's plan would end state incentives, make developers pay all grid and energy costs, require public disclosure of water, power, acreage and jobs, ban NDAs, add setbacks and require union construction. Republican Zach Lahn, who backs a statewide moratorium, said Sand copied him.
iw: Both nominees now target incentives

t: Byrnes loses Senate primary after making data centers her defining issue
b: Cattlemen's Association executive Mike Deering beat Rep. Tricia Byrnes 56% to 44% for the GOP nomination in the 10th District, home to the Amazon and Google campuses near New Florence. Byrnes had branded him Data Center Deering; he says projects need strong guardrails, transparency and ratepayer protection.
iw: Leading moratorium advocate loses in the host district

t: Heinrich introduces GRID Savings Act making large data centers pay for grid upgrades
b: The Senate Energy committee's top Democrat introduced a bill directing FERC to make hyperscale users, 150 megawatts or more, fund the grid upgrades they require. Heinrich said he is not a fan of the moratorium approach because it could push projects to places with weaker standards.
iw: Developers would bear grid-upgrade costs; he opposes moratoria

t: Marshall adopts one-year data center moratorium amid threats to council
b: The council approved a one-year pause on new data center development; police later warned members of a credible threat tied to the debate over a proposed project. Wixom is separately rewriting zoning during its own 180-day moratorium.
iw: Pause in a city courted for a large project

t: Jeffersonville adopts one-year data center moratorium outside River Ridge
b: The council lengthened a proposed six-month pause to a year and suspended rules to pass it immediately so no application could slip in. It exempts River Ridge Commerce Center and Meta's nearly finished campus there. New Albany had unanimously adopted a one-year pause in July.
iw: Southern Indiana cities pausing outside industrial parks

t: Elk River adopts one-year data center moratorium
b: The unanimous interim ordinance prohibits all data center development, including zoning and land-use requests, for a year while staff study what a permanent ordinance should contain. It follows the council's July rejection of a proposed conversion project.
iw: Full one-year prohibition

t: Hastings advances one-year data center moratorium with no proposals pending
b: The council passed first reading of an interim ordinance halting data center projects while staff study infrastructure and energy impacts and define the use in city code. Staff said the city has no pending interest and lacks hyperscale acreage. A hearing and final vote were set for later in August.
iw: Pre-emptive pause moving toward adoption

t: North Mankato tables data center moratorium to tighten its language
b: After a hearing where most of 15 speakers backed a pause but called the draft too broad, the council delayed its vote two weeks. The proposal would halt new data centers for up to 12 months, renewable once; residents urged lower size, water and power thresholds.
iw: Pause likely, with stricter thresholds sought

t: Town of Janesville enacts a yearlong data center moratorium after packed hearing
b: The board approved the pause a week after its planning and zoning committee recommended it at a hearing. No formal proposal exists, but a San Diego firm wrote in April about farmland at North Polzin and West Fenrick roads. The board may extend the pause to finish new rules.
iw: Third Rock County town to pause within a week

t: Rockford votes 14-0 for a six-month data center moratorium, exempting Monarch's site
b: The pause orders staff to review best practices for data center development after months of packed council meetings over energy, water and noise. It does not cover land along Edson Road where Monarch Energy is pursuing a hyperscale campus, because an existing annexation agreement already allows data centers there.
iw: Pause with a carve-out for the one live hyperscale proposal

t: More than 30 New Jersey towns ban data centers by mid-August
b: Includes Jersey City, Bayonne, Howell, Warren, Madison, East Brunswick and Stafford, per an advocacy group's count.
iw: Bans spreading statewide

t: Utility study eyes a large load at Bow's former coal plant
b: Eversource is studying service for a possible hyperscale project at the Merrimack Station site, per FERC filings. Gov. Ayotte opposes it.
iw: Early-stage project facing opposition

t: Project Flash campus in Franklin County is cancelled
b: Developer talks failed after more than 40 speakers opposed it.
iw: Project cancelled

t: Rutherford County committee backs a six-month pause
b: Contingent on legal review and full commission approval.
iw: Possible county pause

t: Alabama counties ask for zoning power over data centers
b: Most counties can't zone, so rural projects need no local vote. The group wants the legislature to act in 2027.
iw: Push for local control

t: Escambia County bans large data centers and targets mid-size ones
b: A July resolution barred them as principal uses and an August ban covered large facilities. A pause on 10 to 50 MW projects is in the works.
iw: County ban

t: Landry says Louisiana doesn't need a moratorium
b: He favors what he calls responsible growth as other states clamp down.
iw: Pro-development stance

t: Montana state senator says her first 2027 bill request would ban large data centers
b: In an op-ed, Democratic Sen. Ellie Boldman said she has filed a draft request to ban large-scale data centers statewide and will not compromise. Draft requests have no legal effect until a bill is introduced.
iw: Proposed statewide ban faces a long road in the 2027 session

t: Woodford County adopts a six-month pause on data center applications
b: The moratorium runs through February 2027, with an option for a six-month extension, while the county holds hearings and writes a data center ordinance. Neighboring Tazewell County's land use committee discussed a moratorium the same week but did not act.
iw: Applications halted in a Peoria-area county

t: Tiffany ad brands his rival Data Center David Crowley, backs repealing the tax credit
b: The Republican nominee said Crowley would give data centers a blank check and called for ending the state credit signed by Gov. Evers, while promising to protect farmland. Neither nominee backed a moratorium at the time; both supported banning NDAs and local final say.
iw: Incentives under attack from the Republican nominee

t: Ypsilanti Township pauses large utility structures amid U-M computing center plan
b: The township approved a six-month moratorium on large electric utility structures while it assesses the University of Michigan's planned $1.2 billion research computing facility on a 144-acre site. Genoa Township separately extended its data center and crypto-mining moratorium six months to finish a noise study.
iw: Slows grid build-out for the U-M project

t: Winnebago County approves a 12-month data center pause in four county-zoned towns
b: The board adopted County Executive Gordon Hintz's proposal covering Algoma, Omro, Neenah and Nekimi, the only towns where the county controls zoning. No project is proposed. The Legislative Reference Bureau had questioned whether counties can impose moratoriums under Chapter 66; Hintz is asking cities and villages to adopt matching rules.
iw: Pause in force, though its legal footing is contested

t: Kenosha residents press the city to pause Microsoft's 240-acre project
b: Kenoshans Unite Against Microsoft Data Center and neighbors have used city meetings to demand a moratorium or referendum, citing noise, water, power and secrecy. Microsoft bought the land in early 2025 and ended its NDA with the city June 22 but has released no plan.
iw: Organized opposition forming before plans are filed

t: Kansas City commission unanimously rejects 20-story downtown data center
b: The City Plan Commission voted 6-0 against Revitalization Unlimited's 384-foot tower atop a historic building at 934 Central Street after 55 speakers and 475 opposition letters. Mayor Quinton Lucas said a council override is highly unlikely. Opponents want a citywide ban rather than the proposed transparency task force.
iw: High-profile project killed with mayor's backing

t: Missouri opposition to local data centers jumps to 68% in SLU poll
b: The Aug. 13-24 survey of 900 likely voters found 68% oppose a data center in their community and 17% support one, up 17 points since February. For a data center elsewhere in Missouri, 55% opposed and 29% supported; asked first, statewide opposition reached 66%.
iw: Opposition hardening fast across the state

t: Chisago County imposes one-year moratorium on data center applications
b: Commissioners halted applications for data centers and other high-utility-use developments in areas under county zoning while the planning commission drafts a definition and conditions. The assistant county attorney said the board can hold a hearing and lift the pause as soon as an ordinance is ready. No project was named.
iw: Countywide application freeze north of the metro

t: Five large Ohio developers donate to utility bill assistance program
b: Five of the state's biggest data center developers announced contributions to a utility bill assistance fund in late August, as industry groups also ran ads in Ohio and six other states promoting data centers, amid polling showing 78% of voters back a temporary moratorium.
s: News From The States (Ohio Capital Journal)
iw: Industry tries to blunt cost backlash before the election

t: Pataskala rejects Aligned data center; developer seeks court review
b: Council voted down an Aligned data center proposal in late August, and the developer has asked a judge to review the denial. Voters in the Licking County city will separately decide Nov. 3 a citizen charter amendment banning data centers with monthly demand of 25 MW or more.
iw: Project denial in Licking County with a ban vote pending

t: Klobuchar backs 2025 ratepayer law; Lindell wants tax exemption repealed
b: Surveyed by the Reformer, Klobuchar's campaign stressed local control and protecting energy bills, while Mike Lindell endorsed local moratoriums, repealing the sales tax exemption and an NDA ban. Republicans Lisa Demuth, later the nominee, and Kendall Qualls did not respond.
iw: Frontrunner defends existing law rather than new limits

t: Town of Beloit follows Turtle, rejects Panattoni agreement and begins 12-month pause
b: The board unanimously declined the cost-reimbursement agreement for the Prairie Avenue hyperscale campus and started the process for a one-year data center moratorium, effectively blocking Project Cornmaze in both towns. The town will absorb the cost of rewriting its zoning during the pause.
iw: Second host town exits the same $1 billion project

t: Hut 8's Logan Prairie campus stalls as Latham cancels vote, county tables applications
b: Latham called off an Aug. 3 annexation and rezoning vote after its president concluded it would fail, and Logan County canceled Aug. 5-6 planning and zoning hearings because the state's attorney found technical errors in the applications. Hut 8 could resubmit for September at the earliest.
iw: Both approval paths for the biggest downstate proposal on hold

t: Residents sue to stop T5's $18 billion Grayslake data center campus
b: The Preservation of Community Well-Being Collective and nine residents sued Grayslake, T5 Data Centers and Alter Asset Management, arguing data centers are not a permitted use and closed-door deliberations violated the Open Meetings Act. They want the development agreement voided. The 473-acre, 1.2 GW campus has a building permit.
iw: Permitted hyperscale campus faces litigation over its approvals

t: State sets a schedule to retire xAI's 69 temporary turbines
b: Retirements begin Aug. 18, but some units can run until July 2027.
iw: Phase-out with extensions

t: Forsyth denies rezoning for the Project Iron Spur campus
b: Voted 5–2 against the 129-acre hyperscale site in Rural Hall.
iw: Project denied

t: Bannock County adopts 180-day moratorium on data center permit applications
b: Emergency Ordinance 2026-02 pauses applications in unincorporated areas from July 30 through Jan. 26, 2027 while staff draft a standalone ordinance. It does not apply to Pocatello, where a separate project is under city review.
iw: Applications frozen for six months in a county with strong power resources

t: Taylor County pauses data centers, solar and battery projects for a year
b: Ordinance No. 40 imposes a 12-month moratorium on new applications for data centers, solar energy systems, battery storage and mineral rights developments while the county works on regulations.
iw: Blanket pause on energy-intensive land uses

t: Turtle walks away from Panattoni's $1 billion Project Cornmaze, starts a moratorium
b: The board voted 5-0 to reject the developer's revised cost-reimbursement agreement for a 2 million-square-foot hyperscale campus straddling Turtle and the Town of Beloit, and 5-0 to begin a 12-month moratorium on developments over 10,000 square feet. The chairman reversed his early-July support; a recall petition targets him.
iw: Hyperscale campus loses its host town and faces a year-long pause

t: Pulaski County rejects a 12-month moratorium
b: Voted 10–3 amid disputes over exempting AVAIO's $6 billion Wrightsville project.
iw: Pause rejected

t: Westerly adopts a one-year data center moratorium
b: Voted 7–0 to study grid, water and emergency service impacts.
iw: One-year town pause

t: Utah regulators hear opposition to Tooele Valley data center discharge permit
b: At a July 27 hearing, residents opposed a state permit that would let the Tooele Valley project, which includes a 500-megawatt data center, discharge up to 250,000 gallons of wastewater daily toward Great Salt Lake wetlands. No decision had been issued as of mid-August.
iw: Key discharge permit faces organized opposition

t: Pillen touts Nebraska large-load laws at White House ratepayer roundtable
b: At a White House event promoting the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, Pillen pointed to LB 1261 and LB 1010, which let public power districts set large-load rates and make data centers fund their own upgrades, and to his new task force protecting the Ogallala Aquifer.
iw: Pay-your-own-way framework paired with continued recruitment

t: Columbus pursues water and decommissioning rules instead of a moratorium
b: At a public hearing, Councilmember Christopher Wyche advanced three proposed ordinances on data center water reporting, sewer connections and closure plans, rejecting residents' calls for a ban. Special utility rates are under study. A second hearing was set for Sept. 16.
iw: Regulation rather than a ban in the state's largest city

t: Augusta extends its pause, but QTS's campus stays exempt
b: The original 49-day pause was extended 60 days with three public hearings.
iw: Pause with a big carve-out

t: Sierra County adopts 18-month data center moratorium after Spaceport proposal
b: Commissioners unanimously turned a resolution opposing large data centers into an 18-month moratorium on July 21, after residents protested a solar-powered data center proposed at Spaceport America. A petition had gathered 408 signatures.
iw: Applications frozen for 18 months

t: Lochbuie approves five-year data center moratorium, longest in Colorado
b: The board voted 6-1 to stop accepting or reviewing applications for new or expanded data centers. The mayor called it proactive, since no developer had approached the town.
iw: Five-year pause, the longest in Colorado

t: Yankton County halts data center and bitcoin mining permits for six months
b: Commissioners unanimously adopted a six-month moratorium on permits for new data centers and bitcoin mining facilities, half the twelve months originally proposed, with a possible six-month extension if no ordinance is ready. Planning and zoning was told to begin drafting rules immediately.
iw: County permit freeze under the new state local-control law

t: Nodaway County enacts six-month moratorium after data center proposal surfaces
b: The unanimous order bars construction and operation of data centers and ancillary facilities in unincorporated areas, extendable six more months. Commissioners want to study grid stability, water, noise, stormwater, emergency response, tax effects and whether to adopt zoning. A developer holds a land option but has not bought the site.
iw: Pause aimed at a specific pending site

t: Monument adopts six-month moratorium on data center applications
b: The town council voted to pause new applications while the land development code is updated. No project had applied. It is the first municipality in El Paso County to adopt a pause, a week after Woodland Park.
iw: Applications frozen for six months

t: MISO tells FERC it will fast-track co-located generation for large loads
b: In its informational report, MISO said it remains resource adequate but promised a zero-injection interconnection agreement filing by late July and a parallel study process for large loads and their generation by late September. SPP said its existing processes already suffice.
iw: New fast lanes for bring-your-own-generation projects across MISO states

t: Walz says Pillen reversed himself on data center incentives
b: The Democratic nominee for governor said Gov. Jim Pillen had lobbied senators for data center tax incentives less than four months before his executive order barred ImagiNE Act credits for data center projects. Pillen said the order is not a moratorium; Sen. Mike Jacobson plans a 2027 bill codifying it.
iw: Both major candidates now oppose new state incentives

t: Morris residents pack council meeting against Tract's 1 GW campus
b: More than 120 people attended and over 15 spoke against the Morris Technology Park, a 343-acre, 1 gigawatt site at Route 6 and Gun Club Road on land annexed and zoned in 2025. A Facebook-based opposition group plans its own meetings after the city held only virtual sessions.
iw: Organized opposition forming around an already-zoned campus

t: Columnist says Emporia data center developer disclaimed project under oath
b: McCoy reports that Gary Pinkston, promoted as the Flint Hills Digital Campus developer, told a federal bankruptcy creditors' meeting he had no interest in the project, contradicting radio remarks. The column faults the city's fast annexation and 6-1 planning vote and calls for disclosure of LLC ownership.
iw: Transparency critique ahead of Emporia's November ballot measure

t: Contractors' group argues Michigan cannot afford a blanket data center moratorium
b: In a Bridge Michigan guest commentary, the Associated Builders and Contractors chapter chief says a one-year statewide pause would likely become permanent and signal hostility to investment. He cites Public Sector Consultants and Citizens Research Council studies favoring case-by-case review with clear state standards.
iw: Construction industry pushback on SB 1018 moratorium push

t: Brookhaven adopts an 18-month data center moratorium
b: Unanimous vote on Long Island two days after the state's executive order, aimed in part at a proposed Yaphank project.
iw: Long pause in a large suburban town

t: Woodland Park adopts 18-month moratorium on data center applications
b: The ordinance halts submission, acceptance and approval of data center applications in the city while staff draft standards. A councilmember said no data center proposal existed and the code does not address the use.
iw: Long pause, though no project was proposed

t: Pocatello council upholds denial of AI data center on former Hoku site, 4-1
b: Council voted 4-1 to affirm the hearing examiner's decision on the $2.6 billion project. The developer filed for reconsideration July 29. The city is updating its zoning code to address data centers, which staff said could take up to 18 months.
iw: Large project stays blocked, with reconsideration or court review possible

t: Marshall says he backs counties that oppose data centers
b: In a KSHB voter guide, the Republican senator seeking reelection said he opposes handing land, water or power to large tech companies and supports counties resisting projects. Several Democratic primary challengers backed a temporary moratorium, local decision-making or an end to tax breaks; four did not respond.
iw: Incumbent senator aligns with local opponents

t: Edgerton council overrides planning denial of DAMAC data center
b: At a special meeting without public comment, councilmembers unanimously overturned the planning commission's denial and approved the final site plan for Dubai-based DAMAC to convert its warehouse into a data center. The commission had tabled and then denied the plan over noise and expansion questions. Neighbors announced a petition drive.
iw: Project approved over planners' objection

t: East Greenbush passes the first local pause after the state order
b: A six-month moratorium on data center development and operation in Rensselaer County.
iw: Six-month town pause

t: Sandpoint council directs staff to define data centers for future city ban
b: Council voted unanimously to have staff propose a definition of data center for an ordinance that would prohibit the use within city limits. Councilor Pam Duquette brought the idea. No ban has been adopted.
iw: Possible city ban if an ordinance follows

t: Cleveland approves three-month pause on standalone data centers
b: Council barred the city from reviewing or permitting new standalone data centers or expansions through Oct. 20, 2026, with an option to extend up to three months, while a working group studies infrastructure and zoning. Existing facilities and in-house server rooms are unaffected.
iw: Short freeze in Ohio's second-largest city

t: Whitmer unveils ratepayer plan and voluntary pledge for data centers
b: The governor proposed rules on minimum payments, contract terms, early-exit fees and collateral so households pay nothing for data center growth, plus a 10-point pledge for companies. It includes no moratorium; Sierra Club called it too weak. Oracle endorsed it.
iw: Codifies cost-shifting protections developers must absorb

t: Logan County becomes twelfth Nebraska county to pause data centers
b: Commissioners approved a 12-month moratorium on data centers that also covers wind and solar systems and cryptocurrency mining. It joined Butler, Box Butte, Custer, Dundy, Furnas, Hayes, Harlan, Johnson, Kearney, Otoe and Seward counties with temporary halts in place.
iw: Year-long county freeze; statewide count reaches twelve

t: Residents from El Dorado, Emporia and Shawnee County rally at Statehouse
b: Opponents from several communities demonstrated in Topeka against new data centers, saying projects were negotiated under nondisclosure agreements and residents learned of them after the fact. An Emporia organizer said more than 1,400 people across party lines had joined; a Democratic House candidate called the issue bipartisan.
iw: Statewide, cross-party opposition organizing

t: PJM's capacity auction hits the price cap again
b: The 2028/29 auction cleared at the $325/MW-day cap with a reserve shortfall. The market monitor attributes about 46% of capacity charges over four auctions to data centers.
iw: Mounting pressure to make data centers pay

t: Jackson pauses data center approvals
b: Covers a 230-acre Saxum proposal, with an airport-area exception.
iw: Capital city pause

w: Commissioner of Public Lands Stephanie Garcia Richard
t: Land commissioner again denies Project Jupiter gas pipeline across state trust land
b: Commissioner Stephanie Garcia Richard rejected Energy Transfer's request to reconsider her March denial of rights-of-way for a 0.6-mile stretch of the 17-mile pipeline, citing emissions and water strain. Oracle said the project remains on schedule.
iw: Blocks part of the gas supply route for the project

t: Asbury freezes data centers for 180 days
b: The unanimous moratorium took effect immediately so the Dubuque-area suburb can study land, infrastructure and environmental effects and write a permanent ordinance. It came a day after Dubuque County moved to hire a consultant to explore a countywide ban.
iw: Another Dubuque-area jurisdiction closes

t: Lawrence imposes 24-month data center moratorium while it writes rules
b: Commissioners voted unanimously for a moratorium of up to two years while planners draft code changes that would make data centers a special use instead of allowed by right in industrial zones. Property owners may ask for exceptions. The study covers water, energy, noise and utility costs.
iw: Two-year citywide pause plus a shift to special-use permits

t: Lincoln County rejects six-month data center moratorium a second time
b: After a three-hour meeting in North Platte, commissioners voted 3-2 against a six-month moratorium, the board's second rejection. Opponents said the county can review projects case by case; supporters wanted time to study water and energy use. Applications will continue to be considered individually.
iw: Proposed pause defeated; projects proceed case by case

t: Oshkosh tells staff to draft a 12-month data center moratorium ordinance
b: Council Member Alec Lefeber's resolution passed 6-0 with one member voting present. It directs staff to prepare a pause on buildings whose primary use is data storage, exempting ordinary server rooms, and to coordinate with neighboring governments. The ordinance returns within 60 days. No project is proposed in the city.
iw: Pause ordered up but not yet in effect

t: Wausau adopts data center zoning rules with a 200-foot residential buffer
b: The 11-0 ordinance defines data centers, requires a conditional use permit in medium and heavy industrial districts, and makes applicants report water use, energy demand, wastewater, noise and sustainability. The 200-foot setback passed 8-3. The Plan Commission decides permits. No project is pending; the council revisits the rules Sept. 22.
iw: Permit path exists but with new review and disclosure hurdles

t: Recall drive targets three Lincoln County commissioners who rejected moratorium
b: A resident filed recall petitions against commissioners Joe Hewgley, Chris Bruns and Jerry Woodruff after the board voted down a six-month data center moratorium, saying they ignored constituents. Organizers need signatures equal to 35 percent of each district's voters. Bruns said existing zoning already lets the county reject harmful projects.
iw: Political backlash against a pro-development vote

t: Stokes and Davidson counties reject data center pauses
b: Stokes advanced the Project Delta rezoning instead.
iw: Pauses rejected

t: Larimer County extends data center application pause to February 2027
b: Commissioners lengthened the pause on new applications in unincorporated areas while staff draft land-use rules. A county survey found about 94% of respondents opposed data centers locally.
iw: Applications frozen for about seven more months

t: St. Charles County bans large data centers for six months
b: The council unanimously paused developments over 100,000 square feet or 5 MW to study effects on health, water, energy bills and quality of life, and discussed a permanent ban. Members said they may extend the pause when it expires. The city of St. Charles had prohibited data centers in May.
iw: Fast-growing suburban county closes for six months

t: Wisconsin PSC lets We Energies data center tariff appeal die
b: Commissioners declined to take up a rehearing petition from We Energies, Vantage, Cloverleaf and Oracle seeking lower collateral requirements, so the petition failed by operation of law. The April order, requiring 15-year contracts and full payment for new plants, stands.
iw: Strict credit and cost terms locked in for Wisconsin hyperscale projects

t: Attorney general opens investigation into fraudulent pro-Project Jupiter comments
b: Raúl Torrez began an investigation after residents in three cities said their names were used on comments supporting the project's air permit without consent, after canvassers in Project Jupiter shirts approached them. Some elected officials said their names were also misused.
iw: Casts doubt on public support cited for the air permit

t: Missoula County adopts one-year data center moratorium outside city limits
b: Commissioners voted unanimously for interim zoning that pauses new or expanded data centers through July 8, 2027, extendable once. The county attorney said it has no authority to ban them permanently. An application already filed was not covered.
iw: Year-long freeze on new and expanded projects in the county

t: Gianforte signs Trump's Ratepayer Protection Pledge for data centers
b: The governor said the pledge commits data center companies to pay the full cost of their energy and infrastructure. The pledge is voluntary, and the elected Public Service Commission, which sets utility rates, is not bound by it.
iw: Signals developers will be expected to pay their own way

t: New Jersey puts data centers in their own rate class
b: P.L.2026 c.32 covers new and existing data centers of 50 MW or more, requiring them to pay for their energy and grid upgrades and commit to 85% take-or-pay for ten years.
iw: Binding cost rules, including for existing sites

t: Grand County adopts 180-day pause on data center applications
b: Commissioners voted unanimously on July 7 for a temporary regulation while permanent standards are written. No applications were pending. Staff said a mid-scale data center could need two to four times the county's yearly electricity use.
iw: New applications frozen for six months

t: Broomfield adopts 18-month moratorium on data centers of 10 megawatts or more
b: The council voted unanimously to bar new or expanded facilities at that size through December 2027, or until regulations pass. Existing centers are unaffected.
iw: Long pause on new projects of meaningful size

t: Neosho adopts one-year moratorium on data center construction
b: The council unanimously paused construction for up to a year, or less if research finishes sooner, to study effects on property values, residents, water and power. The vote came as Geronimo Power floated a data center park with a 2,000-acre solar farm north of Sarcoxie in neighboring Jasper County.
iw: Full one-year construction ban

t: Bonner property owner withdraws support for Krambu data center after opposition
b: The industrial park's manager withdrew his signature from the special exception application after hearing public concerns, halting a 7-megawatt first phase that could grow to 29. The county moratorium would not have covered the filed application.
iw: Opposition cost a proposed project its site

t: Residents sue to overturn Sangamon County's approval of CyrusOne's campus
b: Neighbors of the 280-acre Talkington Township site challenge the board's 17-10 April conditional-use vote, saying the petition was incomplete and utility will-serve letters referred to a different, smaller project. The county asked Judge Adam Giganti to dismiss; an Oct. 9 hearing was postponed with no new date.
iw: Approved hyperscale project faces litigation risk

t: Elk River refuses zoning change for 60,000-square-foot data center
b: The council rejected an ordinance amendment that would have let Elk River Capital and Swervo Development convert an industrial building into a data center, and directed staff to draft a one-year moratorium. The related conditional-use permit was expected to be denied in August.
iw: Project blocked and a pause ordered up

t: Hermantown advances Google project with new reimbursement agreements
b: Councilors approved $200,000 more from Mortenson for planning and $20,000 from Minnesota Power so the city can run an environmental review of a transmission line to the site, after a closed session on lawsuits over the project. Dozens of residents objected to the process.
iw: City keeps processing the project amid litigation

t: Independence pauses new data centers for 180 days but exempts Nebius and Patmos
b: The unanimous resolution halts new data center and battery storage projects while zoning is updated. It does not cover the 1.2 GW Nebius campus approved in March or Patmos's pending 50 MW warehouse application; the sponsor said applying it to projects in progress would not survive a court challenge.
iw: Pause spares the two active projects

t: West Chicago pauses data center and battery storage approvals for 180 days
b: The council voted 12-0 for Ordinance 26-O-0011, halting new applications and approvals in all zoning districts while staff draft rules. A Colovore liquid-cooled facility already under construction on West Washington Street, approved by right in 2024, is unaffected. Mayor Daniel Bovey cited an explosion of inquiries.
iw: Six-month freeze in a DuPage County data center market

t: Texas Township 12-month data center moratorium takes effect
b: The Kalamazoo County township joined neighboring Portage and Oshtemo Township in pausing data center development while its planning commission studies farmland, rural zoning, infrastructure capacity, noise and light.
iw: Kalamazoo area now largely closed to new projects

t: QTS terminates the 2,100-acre Digital Gateway near Manassas
b: A judge voided the rezonings in 2025 over flawed hearing notices, and an appeals court agreed in March.
iw: Largest proposed corridor killed

w: Reps. Chávez, Lara Cadena, Rubio and Sen. Hamblen
t: Four Democratic lawmakers plan statewide data center moratorium bill for 2027
b: Four Democratic legislators said they will push in the 2027 session for a pause on new large-scale data centers until rules cover water, energy and other impacts, paired with a bill to close the microgrid loophole. Legislation has not been drafted.
iw: Possible first statewide pause, still only a plan

t: Phoenix council vacates easements for Ahwatukee data center despite resident objections
b: The 8-1 vote on routine easements for Menlo's five-building campus came as neighbors urged a delay. Officials said the site was already zoned and exempt from Phoenix's newer data center rules, and that the vote did not approve the project.
iw: Clears a step for a project already entitled

t: Linn County stops EU-3 data center rezonings through January 2028
b: The board, with Sami Scheetz opposed, will not accept applications to rezone unincorporated land to the EU-3 Large-Scale Data Center District until 11:59 p.m. Jan. 1, 2028, unless it acts sooner, saying its February ordinance predated new information on cumulative water, grid, road and emergency impacts. Cities are not covered.
iw: Rezoning freeze next to the Cedar Rapids campuses

t: Seneca Nation and Sierra Club sue over the STAMP zoning agreement
b: The suit says a deal barring the Town of Alabama from changing its zoning without the county agency's approval is void. A $19.4 billion, 500 MW Stream campus is under review there.
iw: Could unwind the zoning a major campus relies on

t: New Haven considers a 12-month data center moratorium
b: A working group would recommend zoning standards within six months.
iw: Possible city pause

t: Federal suit over Amazon's Louisa site moves forward
b: A neighbor alleges brown tap water, dust and noise from the Northeast Creek campus.
iw: Litigation risk

t: 68% of Florida voters oppose an AI data center in their community
