b: Only 28% support one, with energy, bills, noise and water the top concerns.
iw: Strong opposition

t: Sarasota County and Lakeland adopt one-year pauses
b: Lakeland's took effect after a final reading Aug. 3.
iw: Local pauses

t: Wyoming PSC rejects Anschutz request to treat Carbon County power project as non-utility
b: The commission declined to declare that a direct power-to-customer project on the Overland Trail Ranch is not a public utility, which would have carved it out of Rocky Mountain Power's territory. Developers have eyed such projects for data centers.
iw: Limits one route for data centers to buy off-grid power

t: Three in four Wisconsin voters say data center costs outweigh benefits
b: The July survey of 838 registered voters found 76% saying costs outweigh benefits, up from 55% in October 2025. Majorities of Republicans (67%), independents (71%) and Democrats (88%) agreed, though only 5% called data centers their top issue.
iw: Bipartisan opposition hardening in a key state

t: Kehoe refuses special session, says SB 4 already protects ratepayers
b: The governor said on 93.9 The Eagle he will not call lawmakers back, arguing the 2025 law already makes large users pay for their power and that siting is a local decision. The House scheduled a September hearing on transparency and public-comment rules instead.
iw: No new statewide restrictions before 2027 session

t: PSC approves power project for Applied Digital's Polaris Forge 2 near Harwood
b: Regulators approved a roughly $110 million power project serving Applied Digital's second Polaris Forge campus in Cass County, described as nearing completion. The company's Ellendale campus energized another 75 MW the same month and pre-leased a 430 MW third campus to a hyperscale customer in May.
iw: State approval keeps a hyperscale buildout on schedule

t: Braun order directs state to seek reopening or retaining coal plants
b: An executive order directs the Secretary of Energy and Natural Resources to look for opportunities to reopen retired coal plants or keep units from retiring, which Sierra Club says is aimed at powering proposed AI data centers. The order itself does not name data centers.
iw: State pushes supply-side support for large loads

t: Santa Fe County adopts 18-month moratorium on data centers over one megawatt
b: Commissioners voted unanimously June 30 to pause permits for data centers using one megawatt or more while staff write rules on water, energy and noise. The threshold was cut from 100 megawatts. No project was pending.
iw: Permits frozen for 18 months at a very low threshold

t: Logan adopts 180-day moratorium on data centers and data center power plants
b: The municipal council voted unanimously on June 30 to stop accepting or approving applications while staff study rules. The pause runs to Dec. 30. Draft rules would cap standalone sites at about eight acres and bar hyperscale facilities; they need further votes.
iw: Applications frozen for six months

t: Seward County pauses data center permits and construction for a year
b: Commissioners unanimously adopted a 12-month pause on all data center construction, permits and special-use conditions, with two members absent. The pause stays in effect unless the planning board and commissioners adopt data center regulations before it ends.
iw: Twelve-month county-wide freeze

t: Springfield adopts 120-day administrative delay on data center development
b: The council approved a pause so staff can review existing regulations, analyze land use compatibility, electric, water, wastewater, noise and air impacts, and build a public-interest evaluation framework with open houses. Recommendations go to the Planning and Zoning Commission and council. No specific project was named.
iw: Third-largest city pauses while writing rules

t: Kansas Reflector columnist urges moratorium after Emporia hearing draws 400
b: McCoy describes a six-hour Emporia planning hearing on the 1,000-acre Flint Hills Digital Campus where speakers ran about five to one against, notes the developer's recent Chapter 11 filing, and argues local governments lack the expertise to set safety rules, so a pause is needed until national standards exist.
iw: Statewide column backing a pause amid Emporia fight

t: Polis says Colorado needs data centers if rates and water use are protected
b: In an on-stage Axios interview at the Aspen Ideas Festival, the governor said data centers are needed if they lower utility rates and fit water use. He said the backlash is aimed more at AI itself than at the facilities.
iw: Governor open to projects that meet conditions

t: Inver Grove Heights passes one-year moratorium despite $150 million lawsuit threat
b: The council voted 3-2 at an early-morning meeting to pause data center construction while studying grid and environmental impacts. Florida-based QLevr, proposing a 5 MW, 55,000-square-foot facility on Carmen Avenue, had warned of damages over $150 million. Residents also petitioned for an environmental review.
iw: Pause adopted over explicit litigation threat

t: House votes 197–5 to repeal the data center sales tax break
b: The exemption is projected to cost $517 million a year by 2030. The Senate added similar language to a tax bill, and the House also passed a pause bill.
iw: Could end a major incentive

t: Healey stops accepting data center sales tax exemption applications
b: Paused the 2024 incentive and issued a framework of expectations on cost, water and community engagement, later made binding by Executive Order 658.
iw: Incentive paused indefinitely

t: Minneapolis adopts six-month pause on large data centers
b: The ordinance blocks new, re-established or expanded data centers and related zoning and building permits while planning staff study impacts; downtown projects under 350,000 square feet are exempt. The council must revisit it by Nov. 21. An earlier resolution passed 8-5 in May.
iw: Largest city in the state halts big projects

t: Bethlehem adopts a one-year data center moratorium
b: The Albany County town acted before the statewide executive order.
iw: One-year town pause

t: Clay, Hernando and Lake counties adopt one-year moratoriums
b: Approved the same day.
iw: County pauses

t: Data center backlash helps oust Senate President Adams and two Box Elder commissioners
b: Senate President Stuart Adams, who chaired MIDA's board, lost his June 23 primary to critic Stephanie Hollist. Box Elder commissioners Lee Perry and Boyd Bingham, who backed the Stratos agreements, also lost. Perry said his vote cost him the seat.
iw: Shows the political cost of backing mega-projects

t: Cache County adopts 180-day moratorium on data centers
b: The council voted 6-0 on June 23, with one member absent, to stop reviewing data center and related power applications in unincorporated areas. No developer interest was known. Staff will weigh new standards or a prohibition.
iw: Applications frozen for six months

t: Woodbury County halts data center applications for 12 months
b: The 5-0 resolution bars accepting or processing data center projects in unincorporated areas while supervisors research the issue and hear from the public. It does not cover existing or approved facilities or the 900 acres Salix annexed for a possible site.
iw: Unincorporated land off limits for a year

t: Cedar Rapids clears Google occupancy step as member floats moratorium
b: The council approved an indemnification agreement letting Google obtain a temporary occupancy permit for its first building near the airport, with David Maier opposed. Ashley Vanorny said the city should consider pausing further projects until the two under construction prove their water and energy claims.
iw: Project advances, but pause talk begins

t: Carbondale adopts a one-year hold on data center development
b: The council voted 4-1 for a resolution pausing new data centers while staff study impacts and draft zoning rules; council member Nancy Maxwell wanted more study and state action first. Mayor Caroline Harvey called it proactive, since no developer had approached the city. Residents cited water, power and noise.
iw: Pre-emptive twelve-month pause in southern Illinois

t: Janesville lets Viridian's GM-site data center agreement lapse, orders guardrails
b: The council unanimously refused a 60-day extension of its letter of intent with Viridian Acquisitions for a hyperscale project at the former GM/JATCO plant and directed staff to draft a data center ordinance. An amendment to halt all developer talks until rules exist failed 4-3. Nearly every speaker opposed renewal.
iw: Hyperscale talks at the city's biggest site are over

t: Jackson County halts data center and battery storage applications for 180 days
b: Legislators voted 8-0 to stop processing land use applications for data centers and battery energy storage systems while the county writes safety standards, setbacks from homes and stronger public notice rules. County Executive Phil LeVota said he has supported a pause; projects already underway are not expected to be affected.
iw: Kansas City's home county freezes new applications

t: Montana Democrats adopt two-year data center moratorium plank at convention
b: Delegates voted at the June 20 state convention to support a two-year moratorium on data center projects as a party platform plank. The plank is a political position, not law.
iw: A major party now backs a statewide pause

t: Hobbs vetoes bill letting referendum petitioners withdraw, tied to Marana data center fight
b: HB 2873 would have let citizens withdraw referendum petitions before a vote. Opponents said it targeted Marana residents challenging a data center rezoning. Hobbs's veto letter cited pending litigation. A developer's lobbyist had backed the bill.
iw: Developer-backed bill blocked

t: FERC orders ISO New England to justify or rewrite its large-load rules
b: The show cause order preliminarily finds ISO-NE's tariff may be unjust because it lacks provisions for studying, connecting and charging data centers and other big loads, including co-located ones.
iw: New England grid rules in flux

t: FERC orders MISO and SPP to justify or rewrite large-load rules
b: Show cause orders to all six grid operators, including MISO and SPP, say their tariffs may be unjust for failing to set large-load study rules, cost-recovery agreements, co-location terms and flexible service. Responses were due Aug. 17, with up to 90 days of abeyance to draft stakeholder reforms.
iw: Pushes faster, clearer interconnection paths but with cost-assignment strings

t: Kehoe calls data center concerns misinformation at Rolla AI forum
b: Speaking to about 200 people at Missouri S&T, the governor praised data centers' economic benefits, suggested foreign adversaries may be fueling opposition and took no questions. Small protests outside focused on water use and ticket access. Rep. Tricia Byrnes used the event to call for a statewide hyperscale moratorium.
iw: Governor signals no appetite for state limits

t: Logan County's 12-month data center moratorium ruled invalid by its own state's attorney
b: State's Attorney Bradley Hauge said the May 19 pause skipped a required zoning board advisory vote and public hearings, after Hut 8 threatened to sue. He directed staff to accept Hut 8's applications for a 500 MW campus near Latham. The board also failed 5-6 to adopt zoning rules.
iw: Pause that froze a $5 billion project is void

w: Utah Legislature Economic Development Interim Committee
t: Utah interim committee opens bill file to define large data centers
b: The Economic Development and Workforce Services Interim Committee voted unanimously to start a bill defining large-scale data centers in state code. Chair Sen. Ann Millner said hearings would follow. Other lawmakers are drafting environmental-review and incentive bills.
iw: Rule-writing begins; outcome unknown

t: IURC approves NIPSCO's Amazon special contract and large-load settlement
b: The commission approved a settlement, Amazon's special contract and a related power purchase agreement for data center load in northern Indiana, and separately approved NIPSCO's gas and battery resources. NiSource says data center customers fund the generation and transmission serving them and existing customers get bill credits as load ramps.
iw: Clears Amazon's northern Indiana supply deal with cost protections

t: Uinta County unanimously approves permit for Prometheus Hyperscale data center near Evanston
b: The conditional use permit covers a 506-acre campus planned at 1.25 gigawatts. Its 15 conditions include annual public water-use reporting for 10 years, noise and lighting limits, and construction starting within five years.
iw: Major county permit granted, with transparency conditions

t: Superior passes a one-year data center moratorium with no project pending
b: Councilor Garner Moffat proposed the precautionary pause, backed by Mayor Jim Paine, while the city rewrites its planning and zoning code; data centers are not currently a permitted use. Paine said Minnesota Power had floated a Superior site for what became Google's Hermantown proposal and the city declined.
iw: Twin Ports city closed to data centers for a year

t: Webster County pauses data centers, solar, wind and batteries for six months
b: The order covers unincorporated areas while the county, which has no planning and zoning, studies health, emergency response, stormwater, noise, and water and power use and decides what legal tools it has. The county says it does not intend to halt the data center under construction on Rifle Range Road.
iw: Blanket pause on energy-intensive uses

t: State promises a citizen advisory council at a Tucker County forum
b: More than 150 people attended the panel near a proposed Fundamental Data campus and gas plant.
iw: Process, not new limits

t: Bourbonnais becomes first Kankakee County town to pause data centers
b: Trustees voted 4-0 for a moratorium inside village limits that expires Jan. 31, 2027. More than 100 residents attended amid rumors of a project; officials said none was proposed and the pause gives the village time to set rules.
iw: Village-wide pause through January 2027

t: Developer sues Eagan over the state's first data center moratorium
b: Eagan Capital's complaint argues the city lacks authority to suspend data centers and that only the PUC regulates electricity demand. Eagan had denied its interim use permit in May after unpermitted chiller units were found. The one-year pause began in February.
iw: Court test of city moratorium power, outcome open

t: Adams County imposes two-year data center moratorium
b: Resolution 2026-25, adopted 4-0, bars the county from accepting or approving any land-use permits for data centers, including substations and backup power, and prohibits related grading or construction for 24 months unless the board acts sooner. Individual applications may still be submitted for consideration.
iw: Longest pause in Iowa so far at 24 months

t: Council Bluffs unanimously rejects mayor's one-year data center pause
b: Mayor Jill Shudak sought a moratorium to replace 2007-era zoning rules and address water and sewer limits. Members said a pause would signal the city is closed for business and preferred new rules and a wastewater plan handled case by case.
iw: Major Google host city stays open

t: Boone County halts data center applications in unincorporated areas for a year
b: Commissioners unanimously adopted a moratorium, effective June 16 and running through June 15, 2027, on filing, processing or approving applications for new data centers outside city and town limits. The Area Plan Commission recommended it in May as the county updates its comprehensive plan; officials may study an outright ban.
iw: Pause in the county hosting LEAP and Meta's Lebanon campus

t: All six Rhode Island data center bills die
b: Proposals on 30-year tax breaks, cost allocation, siting and water reporting were held for study. No statewide moratorium bill was filed.
iw: No incentives, no rules

t: Edgerton and Gardner reject six-month data center moratoriums
b: Edgerton's council voted 3-2 against a six-month halt on applications for facilities whose primary use is a data center, without discussion. Gardner's council had turned down a similar proposal on June 1. Residents in southern Johnson County had pushed both cities to pause.
iw: Two proposed pauses defeated in a targeted growth corridor

t: Nessel seeks tougher terms in DTE's 1 GW Google contract
b: In contested-case testimony on DTE's 20-year contracts for Google's Van Buren Township campus, the attorney general asked regulators to raise minimum monthly charges from 80% to at least 90% of demand, increase exit fees and add cost-tracking so residents do not subsidize transmission or supply costs.
iw: Pressure for stricter take-or-pay and exit terms on hyperscale deals

t: Alliant-commissioned study says data centers need not raise Iowa, Wisconsin rates
b: Brattle's white paper argues Alliant's Iowa and Wisconsin utilities are insulated from cost shifting because large-load contracts cover at least incremental costs, and that past rate growth stayed near inflation. Critics later cited it as industry spin in the peaker-plant fight.
iw: Industry evidence against cost-shift claims in two states

t: McLean County adopts data center zoning rules on water, power and decommissioning
b: Adopted without debate on the consent agenda, the rules require impact assessments for roads and services, disclosure of water sources and groundwater effects, wastewater and electricity monitoring plans, fire district training or equipment and a funded decommissioning plan. Officials called them stricter than neighboring counties'; there is no moratorium.
iw: New disclosure and planning burdens, but no pause

t: Box Elder County adopts 180-day data center moratorium, exempting Stratos
b: Commissioners voted unanimously on June 10 to pause new data centers and their power plants on unincorporated land. Stratos is exempt because MIDA governs it. Critics called the move too late; the county is drafting land-use rules.
iw: New applications frozen six months, though Stratos is exempt

t: Ohio lawmakers leave for recess without votes to pass data center bill
b: Substitute HB 646, which would halve the sales tax exemption for new projects, require closed-loop cooling, address NDAs and create a data center rate class, lacked votes in both chambers before summer recess. Speaker Huffman said a veto override on incentives was unlikely; the House planned to return June 24.
iw: Statewide restrictions stall for now

t: American Tower withdraws East Greenwich application after a ban
b: The township banned data centers while the Mount Royal application was pending.
iw: Project withdrawn

t: McMinnville adopts an 18-month data center moratorium
b: Unanimous, as a 25 MW gas-and-diesel-powered project was proposed. Coffee County passed its own pause the same night.
iw: Long rural pause

t: DeKalb extends its data center moratorium again
b: In place since 2025, it was extended another 100 days.
iw: Repeated extensions

t: Socorro County adopts one-year data center moratorium
b: Commissioners voted unanimously on June 9 to bar data centers and related infrastructure on unincorporated land for a year and start an advisory committee on rules. It followed months of opposition to a 10,000-acre solar-powered data center plan with New Mexico Tech.
iw: Applications frozen for a year

t: Longmont bans hyperscale data centers above a power threshold
b: The council voted 6-1 to ban data centers whose peak demand reaches 5% of regional grid capacity or 100 megawatts, whichever is lower (about 70 MW). No project of that size had been proposed in the city.
iw: Bans the largest campuses, though none were proposed there

t: West Haven adopts a one-year data center moratorium
b: Unanimous; incidental server rooms are exempt.
iw: One-year city pause

t: Southaven neighbors file a class action over turbine noise
b: Alleges near-constant noise, vibration and property harm.
iw: Nuisance litigation

t: Charlotte adopts a 150-day moratorium, the largest US city to do so
b: Voted 11–0; approved projects are exempt.
iw: Big-city pause

t: Montgomery County grants Google 25-year Chapter 100 abatement for $15 billion campus
b: Commissioners unanimously approved up to $100 billion in industrial revenue bonds and a 70% personal property tax abatement from 2028 to 2052 for Project Spade near New Florence. Google pays full real estate taxes and 30% PILOTs; fire and ambulance districts are kept whole. Residents cite water use and NDAs.
iw: Second hyperscale incentive package in one rural county

t: Developer sues Monroe Township for over $300 million over its ban
b: Moved to federal court in July. The outcome will signal how far New Jersey towns can go.
iw: Tests whether local bans hold

t: Pritzker orders DCEO to stop processing data center incentive agreements
b: Directive pauses new agreements under the 2019 data center tax exemption program from July 1 with no end date, pending a legislative framework on energy, water and community agreements. Labor groups called it shortsighted; environmental groups backed it. Twenty-seven data centers got $983 million in breaks from 2020 to 2024.
iw: State sales tax exemption closed to new projects indefinitely

t: FERC approves SPP conditional service letting data centers connect before upgrades
b: The Conditional High Impact Large Load Service lets SPP, which covers Kansas, Nebraska, the Dakotas and parts of Missouri and Iowa, serve data centers on curtailable terms for up to seven years while firm service and generation are built. It took effect July 1.
iw: Years-faster grid access across the SPP footprint

w: Senate President Stuart Adams and developer Kevin O'Leary
t: Adams demands 75% Stratos cut; O'Leary agrees to halve footprint
b: After Senate President Stuart Adams asked June 1 for a 75% smaller footprint, developer Kevin O'Leary announced June 4 he would cut about 20,000 of 40,000 acres. He had earlier called the request outrageous and did not commit to lower power use.
iw: Smaller footprint, but power demand unchanged and pressure growing

t: Iron County planners approve permit for 1.5-gigawatt Antelope data campus
b: The planning commission unanimously approved a conditional use permit for Pronghorn Development's 640-acre campus west of Cedar City, with up to five buildings and an on-site 1.5-gigawatt gas plant, after months of opposition. The permit is separate from any tax incentives.
iw: Key permit cleared for a large campus with its own power

t: Arizona law lets regulators set minimum bills and contract terms for extra-high-load customers
b: HB 2756 authorizes the Corporation Commission to set rules for very large power users such as data centers, including minimum bills and contract terms, and requires utilities to report on new interconnection requests.
iw: Opens the door to stricter cost and contract rules

t: Dane County bars hyperscale data center zoning permits for 18 months
b: Supervisors unanimously blocked applications and permits for facilities with 5,000-plus servers and 10,000-plus square feet in the 26 towns under county zoning, through December 2027. Modeled on Manitowoc County, it targets permitting to sidestep the state ban on development moratoriums. Cities and villages are not covered.
iw: Hyperscale projects shut out of rural Dane County into late 2027

t: Senate bills would impose a one-year statewide data center moratorium
b: SBs 1018–1020 would pause new data center projects for a year with $1,000-a-day fines for operating in violation; projects under construction could finish but not open. The Republican's package was referred to the Senate Government Operations Committee.
iw: Statewide pause bill, though leadership prefers regulation

t: Residents sue to put Stratos agreements on Box Elder ballot
b: The Box Elder Accountability Referendum group appealed the county attorney's rejection in 1st District Court, arguing the resolutions were legislative. The county and developer O'Leary Digital moved to dismiss in late July; no hearing had been scheduled as of early August.
iw: Could force a public vote, though odds are uncertain

w: Alliance for a Better Utah and five Box Elder residents
t: Alliance for a Better Utah sues MIDA over Stratos approvals
b: A civil-rights suit in 3rd District Court argues the MIDA law strips residents' referendum rights and that two senators' seats on MIDA's board violate the constitution. Defendants include MIDA, the county commission, Sen. Stuart Adams and Sen. Jerry Stevenson.
iw: Challenges the legal basis of the fast-track approval

t: Gordon signs 'Data Centers the Wyoming Way' executive order
b: Executive Order 2026-03 sets a framework directing agencies to protect ratepayers, water, wildlife and communities, require public participation, and expect developers to cover their power costs. It also welcomes investment and cites national security.
iw: Welcomes projects but adds cost, water and transparency expectations

t: Little Rock adopts data center zoning rules
b: Defines hyperscale as over 250,000 square feet or 75 MW. Residents wanted a moratorium on a proposed Google project.
iw: Rules, not a pause

t: Boulder County adopts six-month pause on data center applications
b: Commissioners unanimously stopped accepting planning applications for data centers (and detention centers) in unincorporated areas while staff draft land-use code changes. A public hearing was set for July 2.
iw: New applications frozen for up to six months

t: Effingham freezes data center and crypto mine permits for a year
b: The 5-0 vote stops applications, permitting and approvals for data centers and cryptocurrency mines within city limits and the 1.5-mile extraterritorial zone for 12 months so the city can research the industry.
iw: Twelve-month permit freeze at an interstate crossroads city

t: Brown County committee declines to take up a countywide data center moratorium
b: The planning committee said a county pause would have no effect because every municipality in Brown County has its own zoning. Instead, three supervisors will informally survey local governments. Supervisor Christopher Welch had sought a pause until state rules exist.
iw: Proposed pause in the Green Bay area goes nowhere

t: Allegany permanently bans data centers and crypto facilities
b: Local Law 3 applies in every zoning district. No project had been proposed; the board cited energy use and farmland loss.
iw: Permanent townwide ban

t: Frelinghuysen bans large data centers; Blairstown caps size at 5,000 sq ft
b: The county planning director says 18 of Warren County's 22 towns now have data center protections, many based on a county model ordinance.
iw: Most of a county now restrictive

t: Holyoke becomes the first Massachusetts city to ban AI data centers
b: A citywide ban, as other western Massachusetts cities weigh pauses.
iw: Citywide ban

t: SB 439 dies after amendments to make data centers allowed by right
b: Democrats proposed it to give towns tools to regulate data centers. Republican changes would have required towns to allow them in commercial and industrial zones, and the bill died at adjournment.
iw: Towns keep current siting powers

t: Court dismisses Mingo County residents' suit over data center power plants
b: Residents challenged two TransGas facilities planned to power data centers near Holden and Wharncliffe.
iw: Legal challenge fails

t: Homewood, Cullman, Leeds and Fort Payne pause data centers
b: Springville and Morgan County followed in June and July.
iw: Local pauses spreading

t: Chesterfield and Newberry counties pause data centers
b: Newberry first voted down a land sale to a developer; Greenwood County began its own 12-month pause.
iw: County pauses

t: Steinmetz asks lawmakers to poll on special session for data centers
b: The senator requested a poll on a session focused on data centers, large electric loads and water, calling the governor's order a fast track. Senate President Bo Biteman called a session premature. No special session had been reported.
iw: Pressure for state limits before the 2027 session

t: Tooele County starts review of data center rules and energy excise tax
b: Resolution 2026-18 directs staff and planners to recommend data center land-use rules, an energy excise tax and development-overlay standards. The county said it had approved no data center and has no specific regulations yet. Exact meeting date needs confirming.
iw: Rule-writing under way; no pause or approval yet

w: Cheyenne Light, Fuel and Power (Black Hills Energy)
t: Black Hills asks Wyoming PSC for large-customer transmission cost mechanism
b: The filing seeks a Large Customer Transmission Cost Adjustment Mechanism and changes to related tariffs, aimed at assigning transmission costs to very large customers such as data centers. The PSC noticed the application July 7; a decision is pending.
iw: Shifts more transmission cost onto large data center customers

t: Oracle sues Wisconsin regulators over data center collateral rules
b: Oracle asked Ozaukee County Circuit Court to set aside the credit-rating and collateral conditions the Public Service Commission attached to We Energies' very large customer tariff, saying they could require more than $7 billion in letters of credit for the Port Washington campus it shares with OpenAI and Vantage.
iw: Court test of how much security states can demand from developers

t: Sixteen Missouri House Republicans ask Kehoe for data center special session
b: The letter says development is moving too fast to wait for January, citing strain on water, power, roads and quality of life. A Missouri Rural Crisis Center survey of Montgomery County voters found nearly 85% of 1,461 respondents opposed the New Florence project.
iw: GOP backlash spreading through Missouri primaries

t: Butler County imposes six-month data center pause in six townships
b: Commissioners adopted a six-month moratorium covering six of the county's 13 townships, those under county zoning, as Trenton and other Butler County cities drew Amazon projects. Fayette County later followed with a pause for its unincorporated townships.
s: News From The States (Ohio Capital Journal)
iw: Freeze across unincorporated Butler County

t: Jerome Township's early moratorium expires; projects proceed under new rules
b: The Union County township's nine-month pause, one of Ohio's first, lapsed in June. Data centers are now in development there under land-use restrictions trustees adopted in March 2026, after residents complained about noise from existing facilities.
s: News From The States (Ohio Capital Journal)
iw: Development resumes with conditions in a Columbus-area hotspot

t: Veto of Vermont's data center deployment bill is sustained
b: The House upheld the governor's veto of H.727 by 83–52, short of the votes needed to override.
iw: No new state framework

t: Cox signs executive order setting a 'higher bar' for large data centers
b: Executive Order 2026-03 directs state agencies to apply a framework protecting Great Salt Lake water, ratepayers and air quality, mitigating wildlife impacts and allowing public comment. Cox said it could delay Stratos.
iw: Stricter state review, mostly applying existing laws

t: Box Elder attorney rules Stratos resolutions cannot go to voters
b: County Attorney Stephen Hadfield found the consent and interlocal-agreement resolutions administrative, not legislative, so not referable. The county said repeal would cost guaranteed revenue of $5.4 million a year. Sponsors vowed to appeal.
iw: Blocks a ballot challenge to the project approvals

t: Armstrong warns developers not to raise rates, cautions locals against NDAs
b: The governor said North Dakota's approach should rest on infrastructure capacity, local decision-making and openness. He told developers to work with local leaders, warned against any consumer rate increases, discouraged nondisclosure agreements with local officials, and said regulation should track resource use rather than industry type. He expects 2027 legislation.
iw: No new rules, but ratepayer and transparency expectations set

t: Wyoming PSC proposes rules for non-public-utility power generators
b: The commission gave notice of intent to adopt Chapter 6, a process to decide when arrangements generating electricity for retail customers are exempt from utility rules. A public hearing was set for Aug. 5; adoption is pending.
iw: Could ease off-grid generation for data centers

t: DeWine halts review of new data center tax exemption requests
b: The governor directed the Ohio Tax Credit Authority to stop taking new data center sales tax exemption applications while a joint legislative committee studies the industry's growth. The pause has no end date and does not restrict construction; existing exemptions are untouched.
iw: New projects lose access to the state's main incentive for now

t: Jackson County pauses AI data centers before any are proposed
b: A one-year pause to research impacts and draft rules.
iw: Preemptive county pause

t: Iron County pauses new data center and large solar applications for 180 days
b: Ordinance 2026-13 halts new applications for data centers, their power plants and large solar projects while the county rewrites its rules. One already-complete project was not covered. Planners proposed new restrictions in early October.
iw: Applications frozen up to six months, pending rules

t: Cheyenne council rejects one-year data center moratorium, 8-1
b: After about four hours of public comment, split roughly evenly, only sponsor Mark Moody voted for the pause. Some outlets reported 9-1; the Greater Cheyenne Chamber says the official record shows 8-1. Opponents cited jobs and existing studies.
iw: Pause rejected in the state's biggest data center market

t: Dubuque County adopts 12-month data center moratorium on 2-1 vote
b: Supervisors stretched a proposed 120-day pause to a year for unincorporated areas while staff draft zoning rules, with town halls planned. The dissenter wanted more legal review. A developer had asked the city of Dubuque about water and sewer connections.
iw: Year-long county pause near an active proposal

t: Bloomington unanimously pauses data centers above 5 MW for six months
b: The moratorium covers facilities designed for more than 5 megawatts and requires at least two public hearings before it ends; the council can extend it. Council member Abby Scott said the goal is regulations like Aurora's and McLean County's. Normal adopted its own pause earlier in May.
iw: Six-month freeze on projects over 5 MW

w: Utah Legislature Natural Resources Interim Committee
t: Utah interim committee votes to study data center impacts
b: The Natural Resources Interim Committee agreed to add a study of data center impacts, on a motion by Rep. Doug Owens. Republicans on the panel did not oppose it. The scope was not yet defined.
iw: Study only; no rule change yet

t: Sanford pauses data centers, stalling a 1,000-acre campus
b: A 91-day pause on the Sanford Woods campus along the Mousam River, later extended 180 days.
iw: Pause blocks a major proposal

t: Jefferson County pauses new data center applications and rezonings until March 2027
b: Commissioners voted May 19 for a 10-month pause on new data center applications and rezonings, through March 2027. Land already zoned for data centers through a Planned Development is excluded only if the facility is at least 1,500 feet from any dwelling. Only one such district exists.
iw: Ten-month freeze in a large metro-area county

t: Pocatello hearing examiner denies permit for $2.6 billion AI data center
b: Examiner Kathleen Lewis found Lex Developments' application for the former Hoku plant failed three of seven criteria: public facilities, environmental impact and public welfare. She said power, water and air studies should come before another application.
iw: Project-killing decision for Idaho's largest proposed campus

t: Logan County pauses data centers for a year, stalling Hut 8's $5 billion plan
b: The board voted 6-4 after amending a proposed 90-day pause to 12 months. The developer had promised roughly $65 million a year in property taxes; opponents wanted time to understand the project.
iw: Multi-billion-dollar project frozen for twelve months

t: Wright County bars data center applications in its townships for a year
b: Ordinance 26-2, adopted unanimously after 14 residents spoke in support, pauses applications across the county's 18 townships while it writes setbacks and other land-use rules. The chair said the goal is conditions, not prohibition. Monticello's city ordinance is unaffected.
iw: Countywide application freeze for up to a year

t: Otoe County suspends data center permits for up to a year
b: Commissioners voted to stop issuing data center permits for up to twelve months while the county studies impacts and updates its regulations. Tenaska has optioned land in Otoe and Gage counties. Madison County separately added a special-permit requirement earlier in May.
iw: Year-long permit freeze in a county with an optioned site

t: Minnesota session ends with no new data center restrictions
b: A two-year hyperscale moratorium from Sen. Jen McEwen, a ban on local officials signing NDAs and separate water-permit rules all stalled before adjournment after building trades and industry groups pushed back. The 2025 ratepayer law remains the state's main rule.
iw: Statewide pause, NDA ban and water bills all died

t: Riley County data center moratorium runs through mid-November
b: The county's roughly six-month moratorium began May 18 and is set to end Nov. 12. The planning director says the county wants regulations or limits in place before it expires and has not ruled out an extension.
iw: Six-month county pause with a possible extension

t: Elwood-area residents sue to void Joliet's approval of the $20 billion campus
b: Filed against Joliet and the Hillwood-affiliated developers, the suit says the plan commission notice hid that the project was a data center, the March 19 vote broke the Open Meetings Act, the rezoning is unconstitutional and the campus would draw 150,000 gallons daily from an aquifer.
iw: Approved campus faces a challenge to its approvals

t: PUC approves Xcel's very large customer tariff with stiffer exit terms
b: Regulators adopted Xcel's framework for new loads of 100 MW or more (20 MW if system-intensive) in docket 25-289: a separate rate class, 15-year default contracts, 24-month exit notice, minimum bills and exit fees at 80% of contracted capacity, and direct payment for grid upgrades.
iw: Long contracts and 80% exit fees raise commitment costs

t: South Carolina's data center permitting and moratorium bills die
b: S.867 and S.902 never reached a floor vote, and moratorium bills H.5526 and H.5286 stalled.
iw: No state rules

t: Coalition asks Sherrill to use emergency powers for a moratorium
b: Cited rising bills, water use in the Pinelands aquifer and PFAS risks. She chose rules instead of a pause.
iw: Pressure for a state pause

t: Sabey ends Butte land deal after REC Silicon uses purchase right
b: Sabey terminated its agreement to buy about 606 acres for two planned 500,000-square-foot data centers on May 13, after REC Silicon exercised a right of first refusal on 627.8 acres including much of the site. Sabey said it is still looking in southwest Montana.
iw: Project lost its site over land rights, though Sabey seeks others

t: S9144A would pause big data centers for three years
b: Covers facilities of 20 MW and up and asks regulators to keep costs off other ratepayers. Recommitted to committee in May; the narrower one-year bill passed instead.
iw: Longer statewide pause, stalled

t: Colorado Senate committee shelves large-load data center regulation bill SB26-102
b: The sponsor asked the committee to postpone her bill indefinitely, and it agreed unanimously, after a compromise with incentives fell through. She plans to reintroduce it next session.
iw: Proposed energy and water rules died for this year

t: Lysander adopts a six-month pause amid a 300 MW campus fight
b: Unanimous vote in Onondaga County following opposition to the proposed Ranalli campus. Several neighboring towns reportedly followed with one-year pauses.
iw: Pause aimed at a specific large project

t: Tennessee makes big data centers pay for grid upgrades, but lets them self-power
b: Public Chapter 961 covers facilities of 50 MW and up. It also allows on-site generation or independent power producers with little state oversight.
iw: Cost rule plus freedom to self-generate

t: Colorado committee kills data center tax-incentive bill HB26-1030
b: The House committee voted 11-2 to postpone the industry-backed incentive bill indefinitely. It would have offered long sales-tax exemptions for large investments. Colorado still has no state data center incentive.
iw: Developers lose a hoped-for state tax break

t: PSC approves Meta's Beaver Dam power deal with conditions, orders a standard tariff
b: Alliant's 220 MW contract with a Meta affiliate was approved with termination charges through the 10-year term, a Meta backstop, cost studies, reporting and a Focus on Energy contribution. Alliant must file a public large-load tariff for future customers of 100 MW or more. The chair criticized the deal's secrecy.
iw: Project proceeds, but future deals move to a public tariff

t: BLM fast-tracks federal approval of Project Jupiter gas pipeline across 16 miles
b: Using a 14-day emergency environmental review, the Bureau of Land Management authorized the Green Chile pipeline across about 16 miles of public land and began finalizing rights-of-way with Transwestern. Federal commission review and state-land access were still unresolved.
iw: Federal fast track for the project's gas supply

t: Maricopa County approves military permit for Project Baccara data center near Luke base
b: Supervisors voted 4-1 for the permit required near military bases. The 160-acre plan has two data centers and a 700-megawatt gas plant. Hundreds of residents opposed it, and air-quality approval was still pending.
iw: Key permit cleared for a large bring-your-own-power campus

t: Smithfield bans data centers in every zoning district
b: Passed 4–1, a day after Hanton City Investments filed for a complex near Fidelity's campus. The developer is appealing the town's incompleteness ruling.
iw: Townwide ban, contested

t: Datacenter Transparency Act would pause siting permits for two years
b: Covers facilities of 100 MW and up from August 2026 to August 2028; referred to the Rules Committee.
iw: Statewide pause proposal

t: Box Elder commissioners approve Stratos project area and MIDA agreement
b: Commissioners voted unanimously on May 4 for two resolutions: consent to MIDA's project area and an interlocal agreement transferring land-use authority for 50 years. Large crowds protested, and commissioners said the state left them little choice.
iw: Local consent clears the way for a huge campus, but not permits

w: Pima County Superior Court and Marana
t: Courts uphold rejection of Marana data center referendum petitions
b: A judge ruled the town clerk was right to reject two petitions against January's rezoning, and that the sponsor could not withdraw them. The state Court of Appeals later affirmed. No ballot vote is scheduled.
iw: Rezoning stays in place after referendum challenge failed

t: Oneonta pauses data centers and crypto mining for a year
b: Unanimous 12-month moratorium in Otsego County.
iw: One-year town pause

t: Townships use 180-day planning pauses to write data center rules
b: Pennsylvania towns can't ban a land use outright, so many use a curative amendment to pause applications while drafting ordinances.
iw: Short pauses spreading

t: Harrison Township adopts its own data center ban
b: One of several Gloucester County bans this spring.
iw: Township ban

t: Bills to end data center incentives and set large-load rules die
b: SB 245 stalled in Finance; HB 5469 died on the House calendar. No statewide moratorium was enacted.
iw: Status quo holds

t: Morris pauses data centers and battery storage
b: The posted text sets 12 months; some coverage describes two years.
iw: Town pause

t: Mansfield adopts the state's first comprehensive data center bylaw
b: Voted at annual town meeting in May.
iw: Detailed local rules

t: Judge rejects farmers' challenge to Kuna's approval of 620-acre data center
b: Judge James Cawthon denied judicial review of the 3-2 council vote that rezoned land for Diode Ventures' Gemstone Technology Park, finding no disqualifying conflict of interest. The farmers appealed to the Idaho Supreme Court in June.
iw: Rezoning for a large campus survives a legal challenge

t: House bill would permanently end Ohio's data center sales tax exemption
b: HB 975, introduced the day DeWine paused new exemption reviews, would repeal the exemption effective Oct. 1, 2026. A Senate companion, SB 374, would end it a year later. The bill sits in committee with no hearing scheduled.
iw: Signals pressure to end the state's core incentive

t: Judge halts construction at Google's Pine Island site pending environmental suit
b: A temporary restraining order bars work on Project Skyway while the Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy's case against the city and Ryan Companies proceeds; the next hearing is Nov. 16. State air, stormwater and PUC transmission reviews are still pending for the roughly 500-acre campus.
iw: Court order freezes a flagship hyperscale project

t: Iowa data center reporting and tariff bill dies without a floor vote
b: HF 2690 cleared House Commerce 23-0 in February and would have required quarterly water and energy reports, a separate utility customer class and a halt to new construction until tariffs were filed, but never reached the floor before adjournment in early May.
iw: Disclosure and tariff mandates failed

t: Cap Times urges Dane County to adopt 18-month data center moratorium
b: The Madison paper called moratoriums reasonable and necessary, backing the county pause for 26 zoned towns so an advisory committee can study energy, water and land impacts. The board adopted the moratorium in June, joining Madison, Westport and Manitowoc County.
iw: Major regional paper endorsing pauses

t: Manitowoc County adopts an 18-month data center moratorium, longer than proposed
b: Supervisors unanimously approved the pause after lengthening it from the original 12 months, saying the county needs time to research and write zoning rules for any data center applicant. Three lakeshore towns had already enacted their own pauses. The approach was later copied by Dane County.
iw: County-zoned land closed to data centers into late 2027

t: Duchesne County rejects appeals of Nine Mile data center permits
b: Commissioners denied residents' appeals of the April 2 planning approvals for the Nine Mile data center and related gas, solar and produced-water permits; the first appeal was denied for lack of standing. Appellants said they would seek court remedies.
iw: Permits stay in place after appeals fail

t: MIDA board approves Stratos data center project area in Box Elder County
b: The state authority created a roughly 40,000-acre project area for Kevin O'Leary's data center and power campus. This is a project-area approval, not full construction approval. MIDA can override county zoning. The developer later said it would halve the footprint to about 20,000 acres.
iw: Fast-track land-use approval that bypasses county zoning

t: PSC rewrites We Energies' data center tariff: 15-year terms, full cost recovery
b: Regulators approved the very-large-customer tariff with major changes: minimum contracts go to 15 years, the threshold drops from 500 MW to 100 MW, customers pay 100 percent of their costs, and a capacity-only option is removed. The utility must address transmission cost shifting and report on agreements.
iw: Longer commitments and full cost responsibility for large loads

t: Maine bars new data centers from key business tax breaks
b: LD 713 makes data centers that start operating after July ineligible for the business equipment tax exemption and the Dirigo program. The state must study other incentives and report by Nov. 4.
iw: Loss of state tax incentives

t: Monroe Township bans data centers in every zone
b: Effective May 13. The ordinance says no prior approval vests a right to build one, closing a warehouse-to-data-center conversion.
iw: Township-wide ban

t: Logan Township bans data centers townwide
b: Also blocks existing warehouses from converting, amid confusion over a Route 130 project.
iw: Township ban

t: Kentucky data center guardrails stripped on the session's last day
b: Rep. Josh Bray's cost protections were removed from SB 197; LG&E/KU opposed them. A Democratic tariff bill also died.
iw: No statutory cost rules

t: Regulators fast-track seven more gas plants for Meta's expansion
b: About 5.3 GW in Richland and Pointe Coupee parishes. A consumer group estimates data center growth could add $26 billion in system costs.
iw: More supply likely

t: Juab County planners approve permit for $10 billion Nebo North data center
b: The planning commission approved a conditional use permit for a campus of about 3 million square feet near Mona after a hearing residents say lasted four minutes. Neighbors learned later; in September commissioners were unsure they could cancel the permit.
iw: Major permit cleared with little public notice

t: NAACP sues xAI over unpermitted turbines in Southaven
b: The Clean Air Act suit seeks to stop the turbines and fines up to $124,426 a day. The state calls them temporary mobile units.
iw: Litigation over on-site power

t: Judge dismisses open-meeting lawsuit over Project Blue rezoning
b: A Pima County judge ruled the county did not violate open meeting law in rezoning the land, even though the agenda did not name the data center. The opposition coalition said it would appeal.
iw: Rezoning for a built-out campus survives a legal challenge

w: Idaho Legislature and Gov. Brad Little
t: Idaho law requires PUC-approved contracts for new loads of 50 megawatts or more
b: HB 911, signed April 10, sets a no-harm test, cost allocation and financial security for utilities serving new large loads such as data centers. It took effect July 1 after passing the House 65-3 and Senate 34-1.
iw: Cost-recovery and security requirements for large loads

t: Cochise County adopts data center zoning rules instead of a moratorium
b: Supervisors voted 3-0 to require special use authorization, noise studies, water-use plans and proof of power supply, and to mostly bar potable water for cooling. They did not take up the 120-day pause planning commissioners recommended 5-4 in March.
iw: Clear rules and stricter approval, but no pause

t: Weld County adopts data center zoning code and bars them from agricultural land
b: Ordinance 2026-01 passed 4-1. Light industrial zones need a Use by Special Review; medium and heavy industrial need site plan review. The 50-megawatt figure limits backup generation, not total power use. Proof of water and an electric will-serve letter are required.
iw: Clear permitting path with water and power proof required

t: Westport caps new data centers at 10,000 square feet for a year
b: The Dane County town's board voted 4-1 for a one-year moratorium limiting any new data center to 10,000 square feet, modeled on Madison's and Dane County's measures. Supervisors cited farmland loss and the fight over QTS's rejected 1,500-acre annexation bid in nearby DeForest. One member opposed any size limit.
iw: Hyperscale development effectively barred in a Madison suburb

w: Idaho Legislature and Gov. Brad Little
t: Idaho law restricts consumptive water cooling for new data centers
b: HB 895 bars data centers that begin construction on or after July 1, 2026 from consuming water for cooling unless it comes from a municipal or water district system. It passed the House 58-10 and Senate 32-1.
iw: New projects must use closed-loop cooling or municipal water

t: Idaho bill to narrow data center tax breaks dies without House concurrence
b: HB 897 would have limited the sales tax exemption for new data centers to server equipment and added utility cost-recovery and water-notice rules. It passed the House 68-0 and the Senate 34-0 as amended, but the House never voted on the changes.
iw: Broad state tax breaks stay for at least another year

t: Cincinnati extends interim data center review through end of 2026
b: Council extended an Interim Development Control Overlay that requires planning commission review of any proposed data center, ending automatic approval under existing zoning, while staff study more than 22,000 downtown and industrial parcels and draft permanent rules.
iw: Discretionary review replaces by-right approval

t: Phillipsburg and Waterford ban data centers in all zones
b: Waterford cited its status as a Pinelands community.
iw: Town bans

t: Kenilworth's mayor defends CoreWeave's AI campus at the old Merck site
b: She says the redevelopment replaces lost tax revenue; packed council meetings followed.
iw: Local backing for a major project

t: FERC extends PJM's capacity price cap for two more auctions
b: Grew out of Shapiro's 2025 settlement with PJM. The next uncapped auction is May 2027.
iw: Caps consumer costs; data center rules unchanged

t: NorthWestern asks PSC to approve large-load tariff for data centers
b: The proposal covers new customers of 5 megawatts or more, with minimum service terms, billing requirements, collateral and termination costs, and PSC review of agreements for the largest. Many parties, including DEQ, sought to intervene. A decision is pending.
iw: Minimum bills, collateral and exit fees raise developer costs

w: Idaho Power and Idaho Public Utilities Commission
t: Idaho Power asks PUC to review cost-of-service rules for new large loads
b: The March 31 petition opens a docket on how costs are allocated among customer classes, including new large loads such as data centers. The PUC set a technical hearing for Jan. 19, 2027 and is taking written comments until Dec. 14.
iw: Could raise cost allocation for large new customers

t: Archbald rejects an 18-building campus near Staback Park
b: Unanimous denial of Archbald 1 LLC's 400-acre application.
iw: Project denied

t: Army picks CyrusOne for exclusive talks on Dugway data center
b: The Army conditionally selected CyrusOne to negotiate a lease for a hyperscale data center on about 1,201 acres at Dugway Proving Ground, targeting fiscal 2029. The developer must supply its own power and water; an Army Corps environmental review is pending.
iw: Federal-land fast track for a large campus

t: Utah law requires large new data centers to report water use
b: HB 76 makes new data centers over 10,000 square feet that expect to use 75 or more acre-feet of water a year report plans before construction and use annually after. Gov. Cox signed it March 23; it took effect May 6, covering projects after July 1.
iw: New disclosure duty with modest cost

t: Utah narrows what the state engineer can weigh in water-right protests
b: HB 60, signed March 23 and effective May 6, limits the state engineer to beneficial use and water quantity, quality and availability when judging public welfare. Critics said it weakens protests like those filed against Stratos's first water application.
iw: Broad public-welfare objections carry less weight

t: Judge lets lawsuit over Project Jupiter's $165 billion bonds proceed
b: Judge Jennifer DeLaney denied the county's motion to dismiss a suit alleging commissioners approved the bonds on an incomplete application, though a March 24 ruling refused to stay the ordinances. Yucca Growth Infrastructure and Green Chile Ventures were allowed to join.
iw: Incentive approval stays under court review

t: Over 200 pack a hearing against the $19.4B STAMP data center
b: Seneca citizens and neighbors urged the county agency to reject the campus and its roughly $1.46 billion tax break request.
iw: Organized opposition to a flagship project

t: ICC lets ComEd scale deposits for large loads and opens a data center inquiry
b: Projects asking for 50 to 200 MW post $1 million, rising $500,000 per additional 100 MW, replacing a flat deposit. The commission ordered staff to open a broader ratepayer-protection proceeding by April 23, to finish within about eight months. ComEd has 75-plus large-load requests totaling 28,000 MW.
iw: Higher upfront security plus a pending tariff investigation

t: Joliet approves annexation for a 795-acre, 1.8 GW data center campus
b: The council voted 8-1 for HW Technology Park Development's $20 billion Joliet Technology Center next to Chicagoland Speedway after hours of mostly opposed testimony on health and bills. The developer pledged $100 million for city services, projected $2 billion in taxes and said it needs no water for cooling.
iw: Largest data center approval in Illinois to date

t: PennFuture calls for a statewide data center moratorium
b: The environmental group says development should wait for rules on siting, water and clean energy.
iw: Organized push for a state pause

t: Saline County adopts three-year pause on data centers, nuclear and hydrogen plants
b: Commissioners voted 4-0 to halt construction of data centers, nuclear power and hydrogen energy facilities in unincorporated areas for three years, a period they can shorten or extend. The stated goal is time to write regulations; some members also wanted voters to weigh in at the next election.
iw: Multi-year county-wide pause on new projects

t: Lawmakers approve certification rules for microgrids and data centers
b: HB 4983 makes developers flag projects that would place an inordinate burden on neighbors. A transparency amendment was voted down.
iw: Fast-track framework stays intact

t: House kills a one-year statewide data center ban
b: HB 1265 was found inexpedient to legislate on a voice vote.
iw: Statewide ban rejected

t: Mississippi permits 41 permanent gas turbines for xAI in Southaven
b: Unanimous, three weeks after a hearing where residents uniformly opposed it. Advocates appealed in April.
iw: Permanent power approved

t: Provo council unanimously denies data center overlay for East Bay site
b: The council voted 7-0 against rezoning a parcel for a proposed grid-powered data center, despite a planning commission recommendation to approve. Members cited location and wanted the city's economic plan finished first. The developer may reapply.
iw: Project-killing vote in a Utah County city

t: Senate votes 32–21 to repeal data center tax breaks; House never acts
b: SB 410 from Sen. Matt Brass died without a House hearing.
iw: Repeal failed

t: Canterbury voters change zoning to ban data centers
b: The March town meeting acted with no project proposed, one of several New England towns moving preemptively.
iw: Townwide ban

t: Tennessee bills on permits and usage reporting fail
b: Including a proposal requiring large facilities to devote half their computing to public benefit.
iw: No new state limits

t: Birmingham pauses data centers over 20 MW for six months
b: Unanimous; DC Blox and the Nebius AI factory are exempt.
iw: Big-city pause

t: Utah law limits local incentives for large data centers and allows county energy tax
b: HB 507, signed in March, bars local incentives for large data centers from May 2027 unless they use a state-approved zone or regional authority. Property-tax incentives are generally capped at 60% of new county revenue and never exceed 80%. Counties may levy an energy excise tax up to 6%.
iw: Subsidies restricted and a county energy tax allowed

t: Lea County adopts first data center regulations requiring closed-loop cooling
b: Commissioners unanimously approved the first of several planned revisions for data centers, including closed-loop or similar cooling to avoid drawing drinking-water supplies. The county said developers had approached it over two years; New Era's Caprock campus was announced in November.
iw: Clear water rules set before projects arrive

t: House kills a bill creating New Hampshire's first data center incentives
b: HB 1739 would have offered property tax deals and business tax credits, conditioned on paying grid costs and joining demand response. It was found inexpedient to legislate on a voice vote.
iw: No new incentives

t: Mayes challenges regulators' approval of TEP deal to power Project Blue
b: She argues the Corporation Commission, which approved the contract 4-1 on Dec. 3, 2025, gave away its rate-setting power by letting TEP and the developer adjust rate schedules. A judge heard the case in September and had not ruled.
iw: Legal challenge to a key power contract

t: Senate passes microgrid oversight bill 22-20; House lets it die
b: SB 235 would have held large private microgrids, such as Project Jupiter's, to the Energy Transition Act's renewable standards and barred shifting their costs to utility customers. It passed the Senate Feb. 14 but the House postponed it indefinitely.
iw: Rules for data center microgrids did not advance

t: Bernalillo County sets conditions for data centers seeking incentives
b: Commissioners voted 4-1 for a resolution requiring data centers that want county incentives to offset water use, use renewable power, hire locally at set wage floors and pay minimum taxes. Projects that skip incentives can sidestep it.
iw: Raises the bar for county subsidies, not a ban

t: Environmental law center sues Doña Ana County over closed session before Project Jupiter vote
b: A new Open Meetings Act suit says commissioners paused the Sept. 19 hearing for a closed session without stating its subject, then approved $165 billion in bonds. It is separate from an earlier suit challenging the bonds themselves.
iw: Could void the county's approval of the project's tax incentives

t: Butte commissioners extend Sabey data center land deal six months, 9-3
b: The council moved the closing deadline for 606 acres from Feb. 11 to Aug. 11, short of the one year Sabey sought, and required two-thirds council approval for any final land transfer. Sabey terminated the deal May 13.
iw: Extension was overtaken when Sabey ended the land deal

t: Dryden makes data centers a prohibited use
b: Follows an 18-month moratorium the Tompkins County town adopted in July 2024 after a developer proposal.
iw: Permanent zoning prohibition

t: Pemberton becomes the first New Jersey town to ban data centers
b: The Burlington County ordinance prohibits building or operating them.
iw: Township ban

t: TVA approves up to 300 MW for xAI's Memphis operations
b: The federal utility serves most of Tennessee, which limits the state's say over rates.
iw: Power secured for a major campus

t: House passes a data center cost-shield bill 159–5; it doesn't become law
b: Critics said HB 1063 mostly codified the PSC's existing rule.
iw: Status quo holds

t: Chatham County's moratorium is undone by a developer's challenge
b: The one-year pause froze a 750 MW Eco TIP West project, which sued.
iw: Court limits local pauses

t: TigerDC withdraws its Spartanburg incentive request after pushback
b: Residents had opposed property tax breaks for the project.
iw: Project withdrawn

t: Navajo LeChee Chapter unanimously opposes Page's land sale for data center
b: The resolution says Page did not consult nearby Navajo residents or weigh risks to water and the environment. Corner Post reports the Coppermine and Kaibito chapters passed similar resolutions.
iw: Adds tribal opposition to a proposed 1-gigawatt campus

t: Mount Pleasant unanimously approves 15 more Microsoft data centers on two campuses
b: The board signed off on nine buildings near Durand Avenue and six plus offices along International Drive, nearly 9 million square feet on former Foxconn land with taxable value that could top $13 billion. Microsoft can now file building permits. Residents raised scale and energy concerns; trades backed the jobs.
iw: Largest single local approval in the state clears the way to permits

t: HB 2467 to repeal data center tax break and set water limits withdrawn
b: The bill would have repealed the incentive, required renewable power with battery storage after 2026, and capped cooling water use. It was withdrawn from committee on Jan. 22 and died.
iw: Stricter state requirements did not advance

t: Prevailing wage now applies to data center construction
b: P.L.2025 c.335 covers projects of 5 MW or more starting on or after March 1, 2026.
iw: Higher construction costs

t: Madison bars zoning approvals for principal-use data centers over 10,000 square feet
b: The one-year moratorium stops zoning approvals, building permits and occupancy certificates for new stand-alone data centers above 10,000 square feet of floor area. Server rooms serving another use on the same lot are exempt. The city must amend its zoning code by Jan. 24, 2027, when the pause ends.
iw: Year-long freeze on new data centers in the state capital

t: Laramie County unanimously approves Crusoe data center and Tallgrass power plant site plans
b: Site plans cover Project Jade, a 1.8-gigawatt first phase that could scale far higher, and a gas plant of up to 2.7 gigawatts south of Cheyenne. The campus was later renamed Project Tembo. Future phases need new county review.
iw: One of the largest proposed campuses clears county approval

t: PJM governors and the White House issue joint principles
b: Called for affordability, reliability, market reform and a longer price cap.
iw: Regional pressure on large-load costs

t: Butte commissioners ask PSC for separate rate class for large data center loads
b: The council voted 10-0 to send a letter urging the Public Service Commission to create a separate rate class and binding tariffs for large electric loads, protecting existing customers. The county has no authority over electric rates.
iw: Local officials push regulators toward stricter large-load rules

t: East Fishkill pauses data centers for three years
b: Unanimous vote; the moratorium runs to July 1, 2029, one of the longest in the state.
iw: Three-year halt

t: DeWitt bars data center permits through 2027
b: The Onondaga County town's moratorium cites the state Senate's proposed three-year pause.
iw: Town pause through 2027

t: Olyphant halts new data centers for six months
b: Voted 4–3 while it drafts an ordinance, as proposals cluster across Lackawanna County.
iw: Six-month pause

t: Montgomery's data center ban challenged in court
b: E. Kahn Development Corp. sued over the ban on a former commercial site.
iw: Ban under legal challenge

t: Lowell pauses new or expanded data centers for a year
b: Home to the state's largest data center, Markley's former Prince Spaghetti site.
iw: One-year city pause

t: Westfield adopts a one-year moratorium on additional data centers
b: It doesn't immediately affect Servistar's proposed 274 MW, 10-building campus, which would be New England's largest.
iw: Pause, but the big project is outside it

t: Vermont's AI data center moratorium bill never leaves committee
b: S.205 would have paused AI data centers until July 2030.
iw: Statewide pause died

t: A wave of Maine towns pause data centers after the veto
b: Bangor, Brunswick, Westbrook, Gorham, Gray, Scarborough and Saco approved pauses of 91 to 180 days starting in May.
iw: Local pauses filling the state gap

t: Energy affordability bill in conference could add data center rules
b: The House version would create a data center-specific tariff; the Senate's largely writes in Healey's expectations on clean power, water and community benefits. Negotiators were reconciling them in September.
iw: Possible binding cost rules

t: Bill to restore local control over data centers stalls
b: SB 658, backed by Tucker County residents, never moved. Leaders said changes were premature.
iw: Preemption survives

t: Mountain counties and towns pause data centers
b: Clay, Madison, Swain and Watauga counties and Boone, Brevard, Clyde, Canton and Hendersonville have adopted moratoriums.
iw: Regional wave

t: New Orleans bars data centers until mid-2027
b: An interim zoning ban; Caddo Parish has twice rejected a pause.
iw: City ban

t: Chandler council unanimously rejects proposed AI data center
b: The council voted against clearing the way for an AI data center after residents raised noise, water and quality-of-life concerns. The meeting drew a large crowd opposed to the project.
iw: Project-killing vote in a major Phoenix suburb

t: Archbald creates four data center zoning districts over objections
b: Passed 4–2 with one abstention; no residents spoke in favor. The districts made the borough a magnet for proposals.
iw: Zoning opened land to data centers

t: Lewiston votes down a $300 million data center
b: Rejected after swift opposition. A $5 billion Wiscasset proposal was paused a month earlier.
iw: Project rejected

t: Regulators approve nearly 10,000 MW of new plants for data center growth
b: About 80% is expected to serve data centers.
iw: Supply for new campuses

t: KCC approves Evergy large-load tariff with minimum bills and collateral
b: Regulators unanimously adopted a settlement creating Evergy's large load power service for customers at or above 75 MW. Contracts run at least 12 years after an optional ramp-up, with an 80 percent minimum monthly bill, two years of collateral, 36 months' exit notice and exit fees.
iw: Long contracts, minimum bills and collateral raise the cost of entry

t: Wiscasset pauses talks on a $5 billion data center on town land
b: The select board halted discussions after resident pushback and is drafting a review process with no set end date. The plan also cost the town a $240,000 county housing award for the same land.
iw: Indefinite halt to a major proposal

t: Bessemer rezones about 700 acres for 1,200 MW Project Marvel
b: Approved 5–2 for a QTS campus; the mayor and city attorney had signed nondisclosure agreements.
iw: Huge campus approved

t: Regulators approve a mandatory data center rate class for co-ops
b: EKPC's tariff requires PSC approval of each data center contract. The PSC also approved $3 billion in LG&E/KU gas plants for expected data centers.
iw: Cost rules plus new supply

t: Page council votes 5-2 to sell 500 acres for possible data center
b: The sale to Huntley LLC sets a feasibility period and does not approve a data center. Residents' referendum petition was disqualified on technical grounds, and opponents continue to organize.
iw: Land secured for a possible 1-gigawatt campus

t: LiquidCool plans Maine's first large AI data center at the former Loring base
b: The Limestone project would fill an existing warehouse, with a Versant deal for 24 MW on top of 2 MW already in the building. The company says its immersion cooling avoids water use.
iw: Reuses an existing building

t: Meade County and Franklin reject data center rezonings
b: Both votes were unanimous.
iw: Projects denied

t: Consent order lets Markley install disputed generators while the appeal is pending
b: Residents learned of the order only in January 2026. Their lawsuit says it exceeded MassDEP's authority, and in August 2026 a judge stayed the permit.
iw: Construction allowed before a final permit

t: Doña Ana County approves $165 billion bonds and tax breaks for Project Jupiter
b: Commissioners voted 4-1 after a closed session and seven hours of public comment to approve $165 billion in industrial revenue bonds for the Santa Teresa campus planned for Oracle and OpenAI. The vote later drew Open Meetings Act lawsuits.
iw: Decades-long tax relief clears a giant campus

t: Residents organize after a $5 billion data center plan surfaces in Wiscasset
b: The plan for town-owned land along the Back River became public in mid-September. Neighbors formed Protect Wiscasset, saying little was disclosed about the end user, power source or grid impacts.
iw: Organized local opposition

t: STAMP data center approval rescinded after a Seneca lawsuit
b: The Tonawanda Seneca Nation and Sierra Club sued over $472 million in tax breaks approved without full environmental review. The developer withdrew to propose a larger project.
iw: First approval undone, though a bigger plan followed

t: Tax break revives a Westfield hyperscale plan worth up to $4 billion
b: At a state hearing on the exemption's rules, Westmass called the incentive critical to Servistar's 10- to 14-building plan. The Conservation Law Foundation urged stronger energy, water and efficiency safeguards.
iw: Incentive revived a hyperscale plan

t: New Hampshire lets off-grid power plants sell directly to big users
b: HB 672 exempts generators that never connect to the grid from utility regulation and renewable standards, a path for data centers to bring their own power. Siting, zoning and environmental permits still apply.
iw: Easier on-site power

t: Regulators approve three gas plants for Meta's Hyperion campus
b: Built for Meta in Richland Parish over substantial community pushback.
iw: Dedicated supply approved

t: Chaves County approves Zenith Volts data center campus south of Roswell
b: Commissioners approved the project, which the county describes as a special use permit for a 1,265-megawatt solar facility to power a 300-acre data center. Company figures put the data center at 1.25 to 1.3 gigawatts on an 8,400- to 8,500-acre site south of Roswell. The county offered no incentives.
iw: Large off-grid campus approved without opposition or incentives

t: Lowell neighbors' appeal of the data center's air permit is turned away
b: A hearing officer found seven of the eight residents lacked standing and in December recommended upholding the permit, which the commissioner later did. The residents then took the case to Superior Court.
iw: Agency challenge rejected

t: MassDEP approves eight more diesel generators at Lowell's Markley data center
b: The air plan brings the site to 27 generators and 16 cooling towers, some within 100 feet of homes. Opponents say it was approved without a cumulative impact analysis or state environmental review.
iw: Backup power expansion allowed

t: State reviews QTS request for 98 more diesel generators at Aurora data center
b: QTS applied in July 2025 to add 98 backup generators to 40 already installed. State air regulators were reviewing the application as of July 2026, with a public comment period expected. NRDC cited ozone concerns.
iw: Air permit could limit backup power at a hyperscale site

t: APS rate case seeks over 45% increase for data centers and other extra-large users
b: APS says the proposal makes large customers pay their costs of service. The hearing began May 18, 2026. A Corporation Commission decision is expected by the end of 2026, and rates could land below the request.
iw: Higher power costs for large users if approved

t: Bloomfield commissioners balk at a data center near Bradley airport
b: Members raised noise, building height, airport proximity and lost open space when the proposal came up in June 2025. A year later it still had not been approved.
iw: Proposal stalled

t: Florida's 2025 tax package rolls back the data center sales tax exemption
b: Part of HB 7031.
iw: Incentive reduced

t: Maine law caps data centers' share of on-site power at a Millinocket mill
b: Emergency law LD 912 strips a generator's utility exemption if more than 25% of its capacity serves data centers. It targets the former Great Northern mill site, keeping its on-site hydropower available to other employers.
iw: Limits data center access to cheap hydropower

t: South Carolina's 2025 energy law adds data center ratepayer protections
b: Meant to keep data center costs off other customers.
iw: Cost protections

t: Rhode Island's 30-year data center tax break bills are held for study
b: S0921 and H6097 offered sales and property tax relief for $200 million investments in enterprise or opportunity zones, $400 million elsewhere. The tax administrator flagged weak job requirements; similar 2026 bills also stalled.
iw: Incentive not enacted

t: Montana extends data center property tax incentive to 2037
b: HB 424 extends the window to begin qualified data center construction to 2037 and adds on-site generation and storage property to the reduced-rate treatment. Data center property is taxed at 0.9%.
iw: Longer tax incentive and self-generation treatment

t: Waterford lets NE Edge hand its Millstone data center deal to a subsidiary
b: The 2–1 vote kept alive a 2023 host agreement worth $231 million over 30 years, with building permits due by March 2026. The Siting Council had rejected a key petition in 2024; a project database now lists the deal as terminated.
iw: Kept a stalled project alive

t: Montana Right to Compute Act limits government restrictions on data centers
b: SB 212 passed 50-0 in the Senate and 61-38 in the House. It requires restrictions on computing resources to be narrowly tailored to a compelling interest. It does not ban local zoning outright; how much authority counties keep is unsettled, and local officials say it constrains moratoria.
iw: Legal shield against local bans and strict zoning

t: West Virginia law strips local control over certified data centers
b: HB 2014 lets the state certify microgrid districts and high-impact data centers, bars local zoning, noise and building rules for them, and sends most new property tax to the state.
s: WV Energy and Data Center Tracker
iw: Local governments can't block certified projects

t: Georgia Power can charge big data centers for upstream grid costs
b: The rule covers new customers over 100 MW. Kemp has cited it in opposing new statutes.
iw: Higher connection costs

t: Bill to repeal towns' temporary moratorium power fails
b: SB 163 would have repealed RSA 674:23, the law towns use to adopt temporary building moratoriums. Its defeat left that authority in place as data center fights reached New Hampshire towns.
iw: Local pause power intact

t: Kentucky offers a 50-year sales tax exemption for data center equipment
b: Passed in 2025 and championed by Senate President Robert Stivers.
iw: Very long incentive

t: Oldham County's moratorium drove off a hyperscale developer
b: The company scrapped its project after the pause; the county later extended it.
iw: Project abandoned

t: Louisiana fast-tracks power plants for large loads
b: An executive order led regulators to adopt the Lightning Amendment, which skips the usual least-cost review.
iw: Faster approvals

t: Massachusetts creates a 20-year sales tax exemption for large data centers
b: The Mass Leads Act covers equipment, software, electricity and construction for sites of at least 100,000 sq ft, $50 million and 100 jobs. Certification rules went to a hearing in August 2025; Healey paused applications in June 2026.
iw: Valuable incentive, now paused

t: Kemp vetoed a two-year pause on data center tax breaks
b: HB 1192 would have suspended the sales tax exemption. The breaks remain.
iw: Incentive preserved

t: Mississippi's Amazon law gives data centers sweeping breaks
b: Passed in two days: large tax breaks, eased utility permitting and confidential negotiated rates.
iw: Strong incentives

t: Wallingford rezones to allow data centers in its Watershed Interchange District
b: The town, which has its own electric utility, opened the district to data centers as other Connecticut towns moved to restrict them.
iw: Opens land to data centers

t: Louisiana offers 20-year data center sales tax relief
b: Act 730 sets a low bar of $200 million and 50 jobs, stacked with parish deals.
iw: Generous incentive

t: Groton caps data centers at 12,500 square feet, shutting out hyperscale projects
b: Adopted after a 2022 moratorium, the rules also bar water cooling. A developer sued for more than $5 billion, and towns as far away as Georgia now cite the rules as a model.
iw: Effective ban on large facilities

t: Arkansas's Act 851 limits how cities can restrict data centers
b: Written mostly for crypto mining; Little Rock's mayor says it means cities can't ban data centers.
iw: Limits local bans

t: Pennsylvania's data center equipment sales tax exemption
b: Still in force, though Shapiro's August order ties new certifications to his GRID standards.
iw: Valuable incentive, now conditioned

t: Connecticut's 2021 data center tax incentive is still on the books
b: Offers 20- or 30-year sales and property tax waivers for large investments. Only one company has used it.
iw: Generous incentive, little used

t: Georgia's data center sales tax exemption now costs a projected $2.5B a year
b: Created in 2018 and running through 2031, the estimate is up 664% from an earlier $327 million.
iw: Large incentive in force
